we are creating mobile app for opencode. since on market none of the apps for remote sessions for opencode have same quality as claude's mobile app remote connection, we want to get similar quality and better. we will add custom features too.
app should be built for android have compability for old android systems too. it should be easy to use and intuitive. you need to make a research on these: claude mobile app, ai mobile app, mobile app development in 2026, mobile app develpoment principles and philosphy - good and bad practices, android system restrictions, battery optimization and problems with background foreground services, mobile ui ux principles rules layouting with new phone designs (spacing with top and bottom edges) and scalabiltiy for different devices. mobile app frontend ui ux libraries and schemes. mobile app optimization and techniques, opencode sessions and backend connection code hygine. after you make research for each in the web compile all that knowledge in docs dir for future development. this part is not something that has to be done fast or on surface you really have to dig deep to come up with the good plan. currently we have thirdparty opencode app but it's not that great even so you can take inspirations and ideas from that analyze it down to files and get some good stuff.
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
goals - work from anywhere from mobile without pc, whole pc setup replacement app should be able to do background tasks notifications widget and so on.
rules - make sure code hygine is good, make sure you don't do economy on tokens and resources for this project we need quality and develpoment speed is not important! don't assume something or go with old android way even you have to support compability for old systems we must always research and deal with new android problems restrictions and issues. never compress regress or rewrite plans or mini plans just correct them add things to them and keep track of everything with lists todos reminders. docs dir is for that.
technical - use libraries instead of custom solutions if possible if no library supports what we want or does not fully fit dont be scared to create custom solution for that too. make sure connections will have stable retry failsafe keepalive and ressurection structure. optimize for speed and quality. keep code smart nice good code hygine good mobile dev practices and easy to read for humans. be brief short elegant but dont miss or overshorten things. come up with the stack in the plan and consult with me. try to avoid firebase or paid things all goes onprem. use blackwall for server and my cloudflare domain uchabokeria.space. don't use tailscale!
development - make sure ui ux looks nice screenshot it or something, build everything with theme system so we can give users option to change themes design their own theme schemes later change variables font sizes fonts colors dynaimically, add dark light mode and default theme (default dark cyberpunk like neon colors). keep project root nice and clean only md agents.md other mds and things for you goes in docs dir. all that happens in mobile dir (and docs dir inside not parent where i startedd session). flow -> first you make a research dump a lot of information and organize it -> you query me to consult ask me questions think hard -> then you create plan -> you consult with me -> we add or correct things -> we go back and forth -> you keep all the plan in docs/grand-plan.md (save acutal file and always instruct with it dont drift from it) which must be main source of truth to other smaller plans -> you create agents.md based on that (don't overpopulate agents.md but also don't miss wiring important information there) -> you write specs for implementation -> you implement -> you test it simulate smoke test verify your work cross check against grand-plan fix if found something -> i review first give you corrections or approve it -> i review test it in my work we fix things if found.
NEVER DRIFT OR REGRESS OR COMPACT OR REWRITE WHOLE grand-plan.md!
app name - opencode remote (put just opencode on android screen). on first open it should ask for all permissions we need you can be aggresive as long as our features work full quality.
this is first message it's something that you have break down analyze don't miss or overlook even smallest details or one word everything is important in this  message. put it as main guide for the rest of the planning. once plan is done cross check with message what you have missed to add be cautions about missing things. if something is not clear or is confusing you should clarify with me in the planning or in building everytime.
we will need all that knowledge and decisions and important conclusions and other important thigns to be session persistant in knowledge base use memory simple memory and .remember
analyze everything well first ask me questions and start it!

10:     autonomous logged-in work. NEVER any dialog. If logins go stale,
11:     re-clone from the live profile while Chrome is closed.

13:     `blackwall-tunnel` SSH service (local 9224 → box CDP, 9226 → box

15:     task needs the box.

Tip Use the opencode server to interact with opencode programmatically. This architecture lets opencode support multiple clients and allows you to interact with opencode programmatically. <skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by classifying how much process the request needs, then work
through your path: understand the context, refine the idea, present a
design, and get your human partner's approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any
project, or take any implementation action until you have told your
human partner what you intend and they have approved it. This applies
to EVERY task on EVERY path below — the ceremony scales with the task;
the approval gate never does.
</HARD-GATE>

## Three Paths

Before your first question, classify the request and say the
classification out loud — "this looks bounded, so I'll present a short
design here rather than write a spec" — so your human partner can
override it:

- **Spike** — a feasibility question ("can we...", "is it possible...",
  "quick and dirty is fine") whose output is an answer, not code you
  keep. Present the question and what you'll try in 2-3 sentences, get
  a nod, then find out as cheaply as correctness allows. No design
  doc, no spec file. Report findings as a recommendation; anything you
  built stays labeled throwaway.
- **Bounded** — a well-scoped change to code that already exists in
  this repo: a new flag, a small endpoint, a one-file fix.
  Understanding the kind of app is not enough — bounded means the flow
  you are changing is already here to read. If there is no existing
  flow to change, the task is not bounded. Ask the clarifying
  questions that matter, present a short design IN CHAT (a few
  sentences to a few short paragraphs), and STOP. Implementation
  starts only after your human partner says yes to that design — a
  bounded task's approval is as hard a gate as an architectural
  one. No spec file, no implementation plan document.
- **Architectural** — new projects, new subsystems, changes that
  restructure how components fit together or alter interfaces others
  depend on. Follow the full process: questions, approaches, sectioned
  design, written spec, then the writing-plans skill.

When in doubt between two paths, take the heavier one. The ratchet is
one-way: hidden complexity discovered mid-task upgrades the path —
stop, say so, and step up. Nothing downgrades mid-task.

## Anti-Pattern: "Too Simple To Need Approval"

Every path ends with your human partner approving your intent before
implementation. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config
change — the design may be two sentences in chat, but you MUST present
it and get approval. "Simple" tasks are where unexamined assumptions
cause the most wasted work. What scales with simplicity is the
artifact, never the approval.

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is too simple to need a design" | Simple means a short design, not no design. Two sentences in chat, then approval. |
| "I'll call it bounded and skip the spec" | Reaching for a label to skip work IS the doubt — take the heavier path. |
| "It's bounded and the design is obvious — I'll start while they read it" | The gate is the approval, not the design's length. Present, then stop until you hear yes. |
| "I understand this kind of app, so it's bounded" | Bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity. A new project has no existing flow — it is architectural. |
| "The spike works, so I'll keep the code" | A spike's output is an answer. Keeping the code is a new request — classify it. |
| "It grew, but I'm almost done — no need to re-classify" | Hidden complexity upgrades the path mid-task. Stop and say so. |
| "They approved the spike, so the follow-up change is approved too" | Each task gets its own classification and its own approval. |

## Checklist

Classify first, announce the path, then create a task for each item on
your path and complete them in order.

**Spike:**
1. **Explore project context** — enough to frame the probe
2. **Present question + probe plan** — 2-3 sentences
3. **Get approval** — a nod is enough
4. **Investigate** — as cheaply as correctness allows
5. **Report findings** — a recommendation; label anything built as throwaway

**Bounded:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, the ones that matter
3. **Present short design in chat** — approach, files touched, testing
4. **Get approval** — STOP and wait for an explicit yes; presenting the design and starting in the same breath is skipping the gate
5. **Implement** — proceed with the normal development workflow (TDD applies); no plan document

**Architectural:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" [shape=diamond];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [shape=box];
    "Present short design in chat" [shape=box];
    "Human approves?" [shape=diamond];
    "Investigate; report recommendation" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" [shape=box];

    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [label="spike"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [label="bounded"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Explore project context" [label="architectural"];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" -> "Human approves?";
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" -> "Present short design in chat";
    "Present short design in chat" -> "Human approves?";
    "Human approves?" -> "Investigate; report recommendation" [label="spike: yes"];
    "Human approves?" -> "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [label="bounded: yes"];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" -> "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural";
    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**Terminal states are path-bound.** Architectural: the ONLY skill you
invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans — never frontend-design,
mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. Bounded: after
approval, implementation proceeds directly through the normal
development workflow; no plan document. Spike: the terminal state is a
reported recommendation.

## The Process

The subsections below serve the bounded and architectural paths (a
spike stops at "present the probe, get a nod"). Sections from
**Exploring approaches** onward are architectural-path depth — for
bounded work, context plus a few questions plus a short in-chat design
is the whole process.

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why
- YAGNI ruthlessly - remove unnecessary features from every approach and design

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design (architectural path)

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
> "This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
````

# Claude Android app — remote-session UX (webfetch-only research)

Method note: grounded `websearch` is unconfigured in this session (`Missing web search model configuration`), so this is docs-first via `webfetch` on primary Anthropic sources (fetched 2026-10-03). No APK teardown, no edits.

## 1. Chat interface structure

- Navigation: the app is a client for both chat and Code. Tap **Code** in app navigation to reach sessions; `claude.ai/code/new` starts a Code session in-app. No separate "Claude Code mobile" app — cloud sessions + Remote Control live in the **Code** tab, Dispatch is messaged as a task.
- Session list: find session by name at `claude.ai/code` or Code tab. Remote Control sessions show a computer icon + green dot when online. Title order: explicit `--name`/`/remote-control` name → `/rename` → last meaningful message → auto `host-adjective-noun`.
- Search: paid plans (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise) on web + Desktop + Mobile can ask Claude to search past chats (RAG, shown as tool calls). Scope: all non-project chats together; each project's conversations searchable only within that project. Incognito (ghost icon) excluded. Citations link back to source chats.
- New chat / input bar:
  - `+` menu next to message box: `Add files or photos`, `Memory` off-switch (must be set before first message; locked after send).
  - Mic icon = dictation (speech→text, text reply). Sound-wave icon = voice mode (full duplex).
  - Model menu next to send button: model + effort + thinking. Change anytime, applies from next response. Enterprise admins can hide models or pin defaults.
- Attachments pipeline:
  - General: `+` → Add files/photos, drag-drop, clipboard paste. Docs: PDF/DOCX/CSV/TXT/HTML/ODT/RTF/EPUB/JSON/XLSX (XLSX needs code execution). Images: JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP. Limits: 500 MB/file, ≤20/chat, images ≤8000×8000, PDF ≤1000 pages (visual analysis only ≤100 pages). Project files: 30 MB/file.
  - Remote Control from phone: photos → Claude sees them + saved under `~/.claude/uploads/` with path told to Claude; other files → downloaded to the host and passed as `@` refs; `@` autocompletes local project paths. Undownloadable files become a `[n of m attachments did not arrive]` note, message still delivered.
- Voice:
  - Dictation: all plans, 12 languages (EN/FR/DE/HI/IT/JA/KO/PT/RU/ES/TR/UK, non-EN beta). Audio deleted after transcription, not used for training.
  - Voice mode (beta, all plans, mobile/desktop/web, phone-first): hands-free (pause-detect) vs push-to-talk, voice + pace picker, model selector (starts on last text model, auto-upgrades generation; Fable excluded), code-switch mid-conversation, transcripts saved as text, connected tools usable (Gmail/Calendar/Docs/Slack), limited preset voices, usage-policy enforced.
- Model/effort/thinking: Effort Low/Medium/High/xHigh (Opus 4.7+, long agentic)/Max; Thinking toggle with timer + expandable section; newer models (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Opus 5) force thinking on.

## 2. Background work, push, widgets

- Execution model: phone never runs code. Cloud sessions run on Anthropic cloud and survive closing the phone/laptop; sessions persist across devices. Remote Control / Dispatch drive your own machine (must stay awake, `claude` running; `tmux`/`screen` over SSH; laptop sleep → auto-reconnect). Project cloud threads run in parallel; local project threads pause while the host sleeps.
- What you can do from phone: start cloud session (repo+branch+task), open thread cards, answer questions, steer, stop subagents/workflows (stops them on host), view git-aware diff pane, watch PRs with auto-fix (CI-fail/review-comment → push fix, reply when ready).
- Push:
  - Remote Control: Claude-initiated (long-task done, decision needed) or explicit (`notify me when tests finish`). Two `/config` toggles: `Push when Claude decides`, `Push when actions required`. Setup: same claude.ai account/org, OS notify permission, open app once to refresh push token (`No mobile registered` otherwise). Skipped while typing/focused on the terminal; `CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE` extends presence suppression. Android battery optimization can delay — exempt the app; iOS Focus/summaries can suppress.
  - Dispatch: own notification when its spawned session finishes/needs approval. Project desktop notifications are desktop-only (browser checks the Overview dot).
- Android widget (Android 8.0+): home-screen, resizable, 3 buttons — spark = new chat, camera = new chat + open camera, mic = new chat + dictation (first-use explainer + voice perm). All widget starts count toward usage.

## 3. Permission-prompts strategy

- Modes from phone (dropdown by prompt box): cloud = Accept edits (=`default`; edits pre-approved), Plan, Auto (only if org allows + model supports). Self-started Remote Control = Manual, Accept edits, Plan — no Auto, no Bypass from app. Local project threads = auto mode where supported.
- Semantics: Manual = approve most edits/shell/network; acceptEdits = + file edits + `mkdir/touch/rm/rmdir/mv/cp/sed` in scope; Plan = research + classifier-approved explore commands, edits blocked until plan approved; Auto = classifier reviews, ask-rules still prompt; Bypass never exposed on mobile. Deny rules win everywhere. `rm` on critical paths, `AskUserQuestion`, org-`ask` connectors never auto-approved.
- Forwarding: permission prompts + `AskUserQuestion` stay open until answered in-thread (telling the project conversation "go ahead" does not approve a thread). Other dialogs (e.g. post-refusal model-choice) expire after 5 min (`dialogExpiry`) to no-action default. Fable usage-credit consent is never forwarded — answered only where the session runs.
- Mobile command limits: `/plugin`, `/resume`, `/claude-api` are local-only. From app use arg-forms: `/model sonnet`, `/effort high`, `/compact`, `/context`, `/usage`, `/rename`, `/mcp` (text summary on mobile), `/config key=value`.
- Trust/security: outbound HTTPS only, no inbound ports, polling + streaming via Anthropic API, TLS, short-lived scoped creds; transcripts stored for sync/reconnect per data-usage policy. `disableRemoteControl` kills it; Zero-Data-Retention orgs can't use it. Trusted Devices beta: per-device enrollment + sign-in <18h, biometric/passkey step-up; blocks local project threads while on.
- Android OS perms are contextual with Allow once / Always / Don't allow: Messages/Email need none (share/intent + in-app preview card, send in destination app); Calendar read needs perm, write via system UI doesn't; Location/Maps, Health Connect need explicit grant; Alarms/timers use stock Clock. Manage at Settings → Apps → Claude → Permissions; Health separately under Health Connect → App permissions. Team/Enterprise lack location tool; Contacts never directly read; Reminders are iOS-only; Health = Pro/Max, Android 14+, US, read-only, beta with native charts.

## 4. Projects vs chats

- Chats: single linear conversations, optionally incognito (unsaved, unremembered) or memory-off (saved but unremembered/unsearched-from). Cross-chat search + shared user memory + citations.
- Classic Projects (chat/Cowork, all plans; free ≤5): self-contained workspace with own chats + knowledge files + instructions + per-project memory/summary; paid RAG expands capacity ~10×; Team/Enterprise add view/edit + org-wide sharing. Search stays inside the project.
- New Projects beta (Code-first, Pro/Max gradual rollout, Team/Enterprise later): one coordinator conversation + parallel worker threads (usually cloud sessions on own branch/PR, auto-fix watching). You feed tasks; Claude routes/starts threads, answers quick questions inline, reports back. Set repos/instructions/memory/env once — every thread inherits. Overview pane: Threads (Ready/Waiting/Working/Landing/Idle/Resolved), Library (uploads + thread outputs), Pull requests, Routines. `Work locally` (`+` → Local tag) runs one thread on your box via Remote Control with an Allow-once folder card (+ optional worktree); needs Desktop `Use this computer…` or `claude remote-control [--spawn worktree]`. Pause stops everything; Archive hides + stops watchers; Delete is permanent (GitHub branches/PRs survive). Enforced cap 200 new threads/day; idle projects cost nothing; thread-at-limit waits and resumes silently.
- Mobile creation: Code tab / `claude.ai/code` → Projects → New project (Name required, Goal + Context optional) or from a cloud session via Continue/Move to project. Local sessions can't convert directly.

## 5. Why the bar is higher than wrapper apps

- Same-engine client, not an API skin: CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, permission rules, connectors, cloud envs follow the session across terminal/IDE/Desktop/web/phone; subagents, workflows, compaction, `/resume`, diffs stay in sync.
- Supervision UX: live tool activity, per-thread transcripts, mode dropdown, in-thread approvals, expiry + presence-aware push, reconnect survival — vs wrappers' fire-and-forget bubbles.
- OS citizenship: Android intents/share/clock/calendar/maps/Health Connect with native charts, resizable widget, contextual least-privilege prompts with preview-before-send — vs wrappers that ask for blanket storage/contacts or paste links.
- Memory/search done responsibly: per-topic memory with edit/delete, per-chat kill switch, incognito, sensitive-topic opt-in with in-chat notices, never-save IDs, org audit/retention/CMEK, citations — vs wrappers with hidden history or no controls.
- Enterprise spine: SSO/SCIM, seat/org policy, model/effort allowlists, connector governance, Trusted Devices, audit logs, data-export parity for incognito — wrappers rarely survive MDM review.

- Remote Control (sessions, push, perms, limits): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control

# Android 2025–2026 constraints for a persistent remote-agent chat app

Research method note: `websearch_cited` backend was unconfigured and direct `developer.android.com` fetches time out from here, so all facts below come from official Android docs via a reader proxy + Context7's index of developer.android.com, plus dontkillmyapp.com. Read-only; nothing modified. Browsers unused (docs task, no login needed) — default would have been `chrome-direct`.

**Headline recommendation (read first): do not design around a permanent SSE socket.** The platform has spent 5 releases making indefinite background sockets impractical: background FGS start bans (12+), mandatory FGS types (14+), `dataSync` 6h/24h cap (15+), job quotas even alongside an FGS (16), Doze deferral, and OEM killers. The supported architecture is **FCM push to wake + short-lived connections** (open SSE only while the chat UI is foreground or during a bounded sync). Details per area below.

---

## 1. Background execution: FGS types, WorkManager vs FGS for SSE keepalive

### FGS types (mandatory since Android 14, API 34)
- Every FGS must declare `android:foregroundServiceType` in the manifest **and** hold `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + the type-specific permission (e.g. `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC`). ([service-types](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/service-types))
- **`dataSync`**: uploads/downloads, backup/restore, fetch, cloud transfer. No runtime prereq. This is the closest fit for agent sync — but see the 6-hour cap.
- **`remoteMessaging`**: narrowly scoped — *"Transfer text messages from one device to another… continuity of a user's messaging tasks when they switch devices."* An AI-agent SSE keepalive is **not** device-to-device SMS-style relay; claiming this type risks Play-policy rejection. ([service-types](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/service-types))
- **`specialUse`**: catch-all, but requires a free-form `<property android:name="android.app.PROPERTY_SPECIAL_USE_FGS_SUBTYPE">` justification in the manifest **and Play Console declaration + human review** ([service-types](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/service-types), [Play policy](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13392821)). Expect scrutiny for "persistent chat socket."
- **`shortService`** (API 34+): no type permission needed, but **~3-minute timeout**, no sticky, cannot start other FGS, ANR (`FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_SHORT_SERVICE`) on overrun. Good for "finish sending this message after user backgrounds the app," useless for keepalive.
- **Background start ban (API 31+)**: `targetSdk 31+` apps cannot `startForegroundService()` from background; violation → `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`. Exemptions that matter to you: high-priority **FCM message**, user tap on notification/bubble/widget, exact alarm, companion-device, **battery-optimizations-off**, `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` (narrowed on 15+: needs a *visible overlay*). Note FCM priority can be server-downgraded if you abuse high-priority without user-visible content — check `RemoteMessage.getPriority()`. ([bg-start restrictions](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/restrictions-bg-start))
- **Android 15 `BOOT_COMPLETED` restriction (targetSdk 35+)**: a boot receiver **cannot** launch `dataSync`, `camera`, `mediaPlayback`, `phoneCall`, `mediaProjection` (and `microphone` since 14). Attempt → `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`. So no "reconnect SSE at boot" via FGS — schedule WorkManager/JobScheduler instead. Test flag: `adb shell am compat enable FGS_BOOT_COMPLETED_RESTRICTIONS <pkg>`. ([Android 15 behavior changes](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-15))
- **`dataSync`/`mediaProcessing` 6h-per-24h timeout (targetSdk 35+, enforced on Android 15+)**: tracked separately per type, shared across all your services of that type; user foregrounding the app resets the timer. Overrun → `Service.onTimeout()` (API 35+) then `RemoteServiceException` crash if you don't `stopSelf()` within seconds. Exhausted quota at start → `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException` ("Time limit already exhausted"). Test flags: `FGS_INTRODUCE_TIME_LIMITS`, `device_config put activity_manager data_sync_fgs_timeout_duration`. ([FGS timeouts](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/timeout))
- **Android 16 job-quota tightening (all apps on API 36)**: jobs started while visible, and **jobs running concurrently with an FGS**, now count against the JobScheduler runtime quota (standby-bucket based). Running WorkManager *alongside* your FGS no longer escapes quota. Debug via `WorkInfo.getStopReason()` / `JobParameters.getStopReason()` and the new `getPendingJobReasonsHistory`. ([Android 16 behavior changes](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/16/behavior-changes-all))

### WorkManager vs FGS for SSE keepalive — verdict table

| Need | Tool | Why / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Indefinite SSE socket | **Neither works** | FGS `dataSync` capped at 6h/24h; WorkManager jobs deferred in Doze, periodic min 15 min, ~10-min execution limit, expedited quota via standby buckets; long-running workers just wrap an FGS (same limits + must declare FGS type) |
| Reconnect/poll while backgrounded | Expedited WorkManager (FCM-triggered) | Survives process death, retries; must tolerate cancel-and-retry design |
| User-initiated long transfer (log/attachment upload) | **User-initiated data transfer job** (API 34+, `RUN_USER_INITIATED_JOBS`, `setUserInitiated(true)` + `setNotification()`) — no AndroidX backport, gate on `SDK_INT`, fall back to FGS-worker below 34 | Unaffected by standby-bucket quotas; must be scheduled while app visible; user-Stoppable in Task Manager kills process without `onStopJob` |
| Finish send on backgrounding (< 3 min) | `shortService` FGS | Simplest, no extra permission |
| Live SSE while user is in the chat screen | FGS started from the visible activity (`dataSync`) or just a foreground coroutine — no background start involved | Timer irrelevant while user is present; stop on backgrounding |

Google's own migration guide says it outright: for background data transfer prefer WorkManager / UIDT; FGS only for "short, critical tasks, or when WorkManager is not an option." ([data-transfer options](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/background-tasks/data-transfer-options), [long-running workers](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/background-tasks/persistent/how-to/long-running), [UIDT](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/background-tasks/uidt))

---

## 2. Doze / App Standby, battery exemption, OEM quirks

- **Doze** (screen off, stationary, unplugged): network suspended, wake locks ignored, `JobScheduler`/syncs/standard alarms deferred to maintenance windows (which get rarer over time). Escape hatches: `setAndAllowWhileIdle`/`setExactAndAllowWhileIdle` (alarms only), `setAlarmClock()`, and **FCM high-priority** (system grants temp network + partial wake lock). ([Doze/Standby](https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby))
- **App Standby**: no touch + no foreground process/notification → network deferred to ~1×/day until charger. An FGS or visible notification keeps you out of idle.
- **Official line**: "if your app requires messaging integration… use FCM if possible, rather than maintaining your own persistent network connection." FCM shares one system connection across apps. ([Doze/Standby](https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby))
- **Battery-optimization exemption flow**: check `PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations()` → send user to `Settings.ACTION_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATION_SETTINGS`, or (if eligible) direct-request via `ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` (+ `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` manifest perm). **Catch**: Google's acceptable-use table says chat/IM apps that *can* use FCM → **"Not Acceptable"** for the direct request; exemption is for apps that *can't* use FCM or safety/task-automation/peripheral-companion cases. Play policy also restricts this permission — prefer the settings-screen intent over the direct request for a chat app. Test with `adb shell dumpsys deviceidle force-idle` / `am set-inactive`. ([Doze/Standby](https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby))
- **OEM quirks (dontkillmyapp.com, re-verified 2026-06)**: benchmark ranking worst→least: Huawei > **Xiaomi** > OnePlus > **Samsung** > Meizu/Asus/Oppo/Vivo…; Pixel/Nokia/HTC ≈ stock. ([rankings](https://dontkillmyapp.com/))
  - **Samsung** (esp. since Pie/One UI): extra "sleeping / deep-sleeping / never-sleeping apps" lists + *Put unused apps to sleep* (re-sleeps after ~3 days even if manually woken; can re-apply after updates). Mitigations to document in-app: disable Adaptive battery & auto-sleep lists, "Don't optimize" per app, lock app in Recents. Positive signal: Samsung pledged that since One UI 6.0, FGS of apps **targeting API 34** built to the new FGS policy "will work as intended." ([Samsung](https://dontkillmyapp.com/samsung))
  - **Xiaomi/MIUI**: background work broken by default — needs **Autostart permission** (`Settings > Apps > … > Background autostart`, MIUI 14+), Battery saver → **No restrictions**, and pin/lock app in recents. There is a community API to *detect* autostart state: [MIUI-autostart](https://github.com/XomaDev/MIUI-autostart). ([Xiaomi](https://dontkillmyapp.com/xiaomi))
- Net: budget for an in-app "background health" screen — exemption status, OEM-specific deep-link instructions, and FCM-registration diagnostics. No code path survives Xiaomi/Samsung defaults without user action.

---

## 3. POST_NOTIFICATIONS + channels

- **Runtime permission since Android 13 (API 33)**: declare `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` in manifest, request at runtime (e.g. `ActivityResultLauncher`), ideally with rationale during onboarding before the first agent reply. ([notification permission](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/notifications/notification-permission))
- **Channels (API 26+, unchanged through 36)**: every notification needs a channel created *before* posting; importance is user-overridable after creation, so pick deliberately: agent-message channel `IMPORTANCE_HIGH`, persistent FGS-status channel `IMPORTANCE_LOW`/`MIN` (no sound). Deleting/recreating a channel resets user prefs — avoid.
- FGS interplay: `startForeground()` still requires a `Notification` object regardless of grant state — design the FGS notification as the honest "connection live" indicator, not a workaround for denied message notifications. (Exact shade-rendering without grant is version/OEM-dependent — verify on target devices rather than assuming.)
- Adjacent API 34+ items for a chat app: full-screen intent now needs `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT` + user grant in settings (reserve for calls, not messages); `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is a user-granted special access — don't rely on exact alarms for keepalive.

---

## 4. Edge-to-edge enforcement (API 35+)

- **targetSdk 35 + Android 15 device → edge-to-edge is forced**: status/nav bars transparent, top/bottom offsets disabled (content draws behind bars unless you apply insets); `setStatusBarColor`/`setNavigationBarColor` (gesture nav) and `setDecorFitsSystemWindows` deprecated/disabled; 3-button nav gets 80%-opaque default. ([Android 15 behavior changes](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-15))
- **Cutout**: non-floating windows' `layoutInDisplayCutoutMode` values `SHORT_EDGES`/`NEVER`/`DEFAULT` are coerced to **`ALWAYS`** — no black letterbox bars; you must pad around `WindowInsets.displayCutout` yourself (top app bar, bottom input row).
- Handling (this is where chat UIs break — IME + bottom bar):
  - Call `enableEdgeToEdge()` (androidx Activity 1.10+) and apply insets as padding: Views via `ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener`, Compose via `WindowInsets` (`statusBars`, `navigationBars`, `displayCutout`, **`ime`**), Scaffold `contentWindowInsets`/`consumeWindowInsets`.
  - Material 3 components (M3 Compose, MDC views) handle insets largely automatically; **Material 2 Compose does not** — pass `windowInsets` manually (`TopAppBar`, `BottomNavigation`, `Scaffold.contentWindowInsets`).
  - Chat-specific: drive the message-input padding off the **IME inset with animation** (`WindowInsetsCompat.Type.ime()` / Compose `WindowInsets.ime`), not `adjustResize` alone; test with gesture nav + 3-button nav + a cutout/foldable emulator image.
- Audit low-traffic screens too (onboarding, settings, permission rationales) — the docs explicitly call these out as commonly occluded. ([Android 15 behavior changes](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/15/behavior-changes-15))

---

## 5. minSdk tradeoffs (24 / 26 / 29)

| minSdk | What you gain | What you lose / keep carrying |
|---|---|---|
| **24** (Android 7.0, 2016) | Max reach on old hardware; multi-window, bundled notifications | Pre-channels notifications (must use `NotificationCompat` paths), no Autofill, no adaptive icons (25+), Java 8+ APIs only via desugaring, scoped-storage/storage workarounds for very old shares |
| **26** (Android 8.0, 2017) — **recommended sweet spot** | **Notification channels native**, Autofill, adaptive icons, `ShortcutManager`, background-execution limits baseline uniform (no pre-Oreo service behavior), Java 8 language APIs largely native | Drops ~7.x devices (small and shrinking share — confirm current figure in Play Console reach stats, not blogs) |
| **29** (Android 10, 2019) | Scoped storage enforced uniformly, background-location split, dark theme, gesture nav baseline, fewer compat branches to test | Drops all of 7.x–9.x — meaningful in some markets; only justified if analytics show negligible <29 share |

- **Desugaring** (`coreLibraryDesugaringEnabled` + `desugar_jdk_libs`) backports `java.time`, streams, `java.util.function`/concurrent APIs to minSdk in the 20s, so language-API level is *not* a reason to raise minSdk — only framework behaviors (channels, storage, permissions model) are. ([desugaring reference](https://developer.android.com/reference/tools/gradle-api/8.2/com/android/build/api/dsl/CompileOptions), [Java 11 API support tables](https://developer.android.com/studio/write/java11-default-support-table))
- **Material3/compat**: Compose + M3 and MDC-Android floors are minSdk 21/19-era — all three candidates (24/26/29) are comfortably above; no constraint either way. WorkManager's `setExpedited` path also covers pre-31 devices via FGS internally, so minSdk 26 loses nothing for the WorkManager strategy. ([expedited work, Work 2.7 release notes](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/work))
- Don't quote stale "% of devices" blog figures in planning docs — pull current numbers from the AGP new-project wizard distribution chart or Play Console → Reach/devices for *your* target countries.
- Keep `targetSdk`/`compileSdk` current independently of minSdk: Play required target 35 (Aug 2025); target 36 enforcement follows the usual August cadence — verify in Play Console policy pages at implementation time.

---

## Suggested architecture (synthesis)

1. **Transport**: FCM data messages (high-priority only when an agent reply needs immediate user visibility) → on receipt, open a **short-lived** SSE/fetch to pull results → close. While the conversation screen is open, hold the socket in a `dataSync` FGS started from the visible activity.
2. **No silent perpetual socket.** If a custom (non-FCM) push channel is a hard requirement, treat it as degraded mode: visible-started `dataSync` FGS, honor the 6h cap via `onTimeout()` + WorkManager handoff, reconnect with exponential backoff in maintenance windows, and invest in the §2 OEM onboarding flow — it will still die on Xiaomi/Samsung defaults.
3. **Uploads/attachments**: UIDT job on 34+, FGS-worker fallback below.
4. **Notifications**: POST_NOTIFICATIONS rationale at onboarding; HIGH channel for replies, LOW for connection status; never conflate the FGS notification with message delivery.
5. **UI**: `enableEdgeToEdge()` + IME-animated input bar + cutout padding from day one; minSdk **26**, target/compile per current Play requirement.

Unresolved / verify-on-device: exact rendering of FGS notifications when POST_NOTIFICATIONS is denied (OEM variance), and current Play target-36 deadline — both should be re-checked at build time, not trusted from this report.

## Mobile stack decision — Android-first, offline, SSE chat, self-hosted, no Firebase

> Read-only. `websearch_cited` backend was down this session (`Missing web search model configuration`), so below is docs-first via Context7 + primary-source fetch + `gh_grep`. No benchmarks invented — relative rankings only.

### TL;DR recommendation

**Pick (A) 100% native Kotlin + Compose**, but layer it so (B) is a cheap future extraction: `:app` / `:feature` / `:domain` / `:data` modules, repository interfaces, Ktor-style DTOs via kotlinx.serialization.

* Only pick **(B) KMP shared networking/domain now** if iOS is committed within ~12 months **and** you have iOS capacity to own SwiftUI + iOS background separately. Otherwise KMP adds dual-platform build/DI/driver complexity for zero shipped benefit.
* Reject **(C) Flutter / (D) RN-Expo for this brief**: both lose exactly where your requirements are hardest — old-Android floor, reliable background/SSE without FCM, VNC/WebRTC native interop.

### Comparison

| Criterion | (A) Native Kotlin | (B) KMP shared logic | (C) Flutter | (D) RN / Expo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Old-Android compat | Best. Compose requires `minSdk 21+` (Android 5.0, 2014) — [Compose setup](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/setup). Room/WorkManager/DataStore all support 21+. You control the floor. | Same as (A) on Android. iOS target modern (no old-device win). Shared Room/DataStore now exist in KMP samples, but version-gate them — historically shared-DB path was SQLDelight per [Ktor+SQLDelight tutorial](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/multiplatform-ktor-sqldelight.html). | Good, then plugin-gated. ### Reasoning

1. Your hardest constraints (old Android + background SSE + self-hosted push + WebRTC/VNC) are all Android-framework problems. Only (A)/(B) give you the full framework.
2. iOS is explicitly *future/possible*, so cross-platform UI (C/D, Compose Multiplatform) buys nothing now and costs startup/size/background quality daily.
3. Theming + offline + chat-streaming need native text/layout performance on 10-year-old GPUs — native Compose > Impeller/Skia-bridge > JS-bridge ordering holds.
4. No-Firebase forces UnifiedPush, whose reference integrations are native Android (Tusky, Element, Molly, Nextcloud Talk all listed on [unifiedpush.org](https://unifiedpush.org/)). Flutter/RN add a bridge layer with no reliability gain.

### Structure (A) so (B) is cheap later

* Modules: `:app`, `:feature:*`, `:domain` (pure Kotlin, no Android imports), `:data` (Room/Ktor/WorkManager impls behind interfaces).
* DTOs with `kotlinx.serialization` from day one — same models drop into `commonMain` later.
* Push behind a `PushGateway` interface (`FcmGateway` stub / `UnifiedPushGateway` / `SseFallbackGateway`) — distributor choice stays out of UI code.

# opencode `serve` HTTP API — mobile-client backend contract (read-only research)

Sources: [Server](https://opencode.ai/docs/server/), [SDK](https://opencode.ai/docs/sdk/), generated types [`types.gen.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts) (raw text fetched), plus [Permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), [Share](https://opencode.ai/docs/share/), [Commands](https://opencode.ai/docs/commands/).

## 0. Transport contract

- Base: `{BASE}` = `http://127.0.0.1:4096` locally, or your TLS URL (e.g. Tailscale Serve `https://archlinux.tail9c9427.ts.net`). `serve` itself is plain HTTP on `--port` (default `4096`, `--hostname` default `127.0.0.1`); TLS terminates at Cloudflare/Tailscale, not in opencode. [Server](https://opencode.ai/docs/server/)
- Spec: `GET {BASE}/doc` = OpenAPI 3.1. Generate/verify the Android client against the **live** `/doc` of the exact server version; do not hardcode schemas. [Server](https://opencode.ai/docs/server/)
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
- Content: JSON REST + two SSE streams. Almost every endpoint also accepts `?directory=` to route multi-project servers — mobile should send it (project worktree from `/project`) or stick to server-cwd default. Verified in `types.gen.ts` (`query?: { directory?: string }` on ~all endpoints).
- Health/version pin: `GET /global/health → {healthy, version}`. Pin behavior per version. [Server](https://opencode.ai/docs/server/)

## 1. Endpoint-by-endpoint mapping

### Global / health / events

| Method | URL | Req | Resp | Mobile use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `{BASE}/global/health` | — | `{healthy: bool, version: string}` | Boot check + version pin |
| GET | `{BASE}/event` | `Accept: text/event-stream` | SSE, first `server.connected`, then `Event` objects | **Primary stream** (`event.subscribe()` in [SDK](https://opencode.ai/docs/sdk/)) |
| GET | `{BASE}/global/event` | SSE | `GlobalEvent {directory, payload: Event}` | Legacy duplicate listed in [Server](https://opencode.ai/docs/server/); prefer `/event`, support both |

### Project / path

| GET | `{BASE}/project/current?directory=` | `Project` | Current cwd context |
| GET | `{BASE}/path` | `Path {state, config, worktree, directory}` | Show cwd |
| GET | `{BASE}/vcs` | `VcsInfo {branch}` | Branch chip |

### Sessions — CRUD + fork/share/abort/revert

| Method | URL | Req body | Resp | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `{BASE}/session?directory=` | — | `Session[]` | List |
| POST | `{BASE}/session?directory=` | `{parentID?, title?}` | `Session` | Create |
| GET | `{BASE}/session/status` | — | `{[sessionID]: SessionStatus}` | Poll fallback when SSE drops. `idle \| busy \| retry{attempt,message,next}` |
| GET | `{BASE}/session/{id}` | — | `Session` | Details |
| DELETE | `{BASE}/session/{id}` | — | `bool` | Delete + data |

| POST | `{BASE}/session/{id}/init` | `{messageID, providerID, modelID}` | `bool` | Analyze app → `AGENTS.md` |

`Session` fields: `id, projectID, directory, parentID?, summary?, share?, title, version, time{created,updated}, revert?`. [Server](https://opencode.ai/docs/server/), types.gen.

### Messages — sync vs async (core mobile decision)

| Method | URL | Req | Resp |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `{BASE}/session/{id}/message?limit=` | — | `{info: Message, parts: Part[]}[]` |
| GET | `{BASE}/session/{id}/message/{msgID}` | — | `{info, parts}` |
| POST | `{BASE}/session/{id}/message` | `{messageID?, model?{providerID,modelID}, agent?, noReply?, system?, tools?, parts: (Text\|File\|Agent\|Subtask)Input[]}` | `{info: AssistantMessage, parts}` — **blocks until turn completes** |
| POST | `{BASE}/session/{id}/prompt_async` | same | `204 No Content` — result via SSE |
| POST | `{BASE}/session/{id}/command` | `{messageID?, agent?, model?: string, command, arguments}` | `{info, parts}` — note `model` is a plain string here, unlike `message` |
| POST | `{BASE}/session/{id}/shell` | `{agent, model?, command}` | `AssistantMessage` |

Recommendation: mobile sends via **`prompt_async`** (no long-lived HTTP, survives radio drops), renders progress from SSE, uses `/session/status` + `GET message` to reconcile. Reserve sync `POST message` for short turns only with generous timeouts. `noReply:true` injects context without triggering the model ([SDK](https://opencode.ai/docs/sdk/)).

### Message parts model

- **Inputs you can send** (`SessionPromptData.body.parts`): `TextPartInput {type:"text", text}`, `FilePartInput {type:"file", mime, filename?, url, source?}`, `AgentPartInput {type:"agent", name}`, `SubtaskPartInput {type:"subtask", prompt, description, agent}`. No reasoning/tool-call inputs.
- **Outputs you must render** (`Part` union): `text`, `reasoning`, `file`, `tool {callID, tool, state: pending|running|completed|error}`, `step-start`, `step-finish {reason, cost, tokens}`, `snapshot`, `patch {hash, files}`, `agent`, `retry {attempt, error}`, `compaction`, `subtask`. Streaming deltas arrive as `message.part.updated {part, delta?}` — **append `delta`** to text/reasoning/tool state.
- `Message` = `UserMessage | AssistantMessage`; assistant carries `tokens{input,output,reasoning,cache}`, `cost`, `finish?`, and `error?` union (`ProviderAuthError|UnknownError|MessageOutputLengthError|MessageAbortedError|APIError`) — model failures come **inside 200 responses**, not HTTP errors.

### SSE event catalog (subscribe `/event`)

`server.connected`, `message.updated`, `message.part.updated {part, delta?}`, `message.part.removed`, `message.removed`, `permission.updated (Permission)`, `permission.replied`, `session.status`, `session.idle`, `session.compacted`, `session.created|updated|deleted|diff|error`, `todo.updated`, `command.executed`, `file.edited`, `file.watcher.updated`, `vcs.branch.updated`, `tui.*`, `pty.*`, `lsp.*`, `installation.*`. Full union in types.gen `Event`.

### Permissions flow

1. SSE `permission.updated` → `Permission {id, type, pattern?, sessionID, messageID, callID?, title, metadata}`.
2. UI shows title/type/pattern; buttons Once / Always / Reject.
3. `POST /session/{id}/permissions/{permID} {response}` → `true`; `permission.replied` confirms.
4. Types: `edit, bash, webfetch, doom_loop, external_directory, read, glob, grep, task, skill, …` each resolving `allow|ask|deny` ([Permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/)). Server `--auto` bypasses asks (denys still enforced) — surface server mode in UI.

## 2. Gaps / risks for the Android client

1. **Attachment upload undefined.** `FilePartInput` requires `url` but no `POST /file` / multipart upload exists in spec. Unclear whether `url` = server-absolute path, `file://`, `data:` URL, or pre-staged file. Must inspect live `/doc` + web-client upload path before building image attach. Highest mobile risk.
2. **No SSE resumption.** No documented `Last-Event-ID`, cursor, or replay; after reconnect, resync via `GET /session/status` + `GET …/message?limit=`. `limit` is the only paging — large sessions may truncate.
3. **Schema drift (v1 vs v2-fork).** Docs banner pushes v2; repo ANOMALYCO fork vs upstream. Revert/unrevert (`Session` vs `boolean`), permission body (`remember?` vs not), structured-output `format` (narrative docs show it, `SessionPromptData` lacks it) already diverge. Verify each against live `/doc`; gate on `/global/health` version.
4. **Sync POST hangs.** `POST …/message` blocks for full turn — set no/short read timeout only for `prompt_async` (204) + SSE; treat sync as optional.
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
6. **Single-server concurrency.** One `serve` per port/machine (shared sqlite WAL); mobile must only connect, never spawn a second `serve`. Your `:4096` + Tailscale setup matches this.
7. **Share = public.** `POST …/share` publishes to `opncd.ai`; require explicit confirm + unshare affordance ([Share](https://opencode.ai/docs/share/)).
8. **`?directory=` routing.** Forgetting it on a multi-project server silently targets the wrong cwd — always send project worktree.

## 3. Minimal mobile call flows

- Boot: `GET /global/health` → `GET /project` → `GET /provider` + `GET /agent` + `GET /command` → open `/event` SSE.
- Chat: `POST /session` (or pick) → `GET …/message?limit=` → `POST …/prompt_async` → render `session.status`/`message.part.updated` deltas → on `session.idle`, `GET` message detail to confirm.
- Approval: `permission.updated` → dialog → `POST …/permissions/{id}`.
- Interrupt/undo/branch/publish: `POST …/abort`, `POST …/revert`, `POST …/fork`, `POST …/share` (+`DELETE …/share`).

# Android chat-app UI/UX + theming 2026 — deep research

Note: the `websearch_cited` backend was unconfigured in this session, so this is built from primary sources instead: Context7 docs (M3, Compose, Stream, Coil, mikepenz), plus direct fetches of [unifiedpush.org](https://unifiedpush.org), [docs.ntfy.sh](https://docs.ntfy.sh), [GetStream docs](https://getstream.io/chat/docs/sdk/android/compose/overview/), and the relevant GitHub repos. Every URL below was either fetched live this session or is a stable canonical URL.

## 1. Material 3 Expressive + edge-to-edge + adaptive + dynamic type

**M3 Expressive.** The current API surface (per [m3.material.io/blog/m3-expressive-motion-theming](https://m3.material.io/blog/m3-expressive-motion-theming)):
- Dependency: `androidx.compose.material3:material3:1.4.0-alpha11` (Expressive APIs move to 1.5.0-alphaX once 1.4.0 goes stable).
- Theme entry point is `MaterialExpressiveTheme(colorScheme, motionScheme, shapes, typography, content)` with `motionScheme = MotionScheme.expressive()` or `.standard()` — set once, all components inherit.
- New components: `ButtonGroup` (connected/overflow variants), `LoadingIndicator` (for `PullToRefreshBox`), wider shape morphing, spring-based `MotionScheme` you can override per-spec (`defaultEffectsSpec`, `defaultSpatialSpec`, fast/slow variants). Custom components should animate with `MaterialTheme.motionScheme.defaultSpatialSpec()` / `defaultEffectsSpec()` so they follow the theme.
- Expressive color: keep using dynamic color (`dynamicDarkColorScheme`/`dynamicLightColorScheme`) — Expressive is additive (motion+shape+emphasis), not a replacement color system.
- Catalog/demo: [meticha/material-3-expressive-catalog](https://github.com/meticha/material-3-expressive-catalog), [emertozd/compose-material-3-expressive-catalog](https://github.com/emertozd/compose-material-3-expressive-catalog).

**Edge-to-edge.** Mandatory posture for 2026: Android 15 enforces edge-to-edge for `targetSdk 35+`; there is no opt-out via `windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement` except narrow legacy cases.
- Call `enableEdgeToEdge()` in `Activity.onCreate()` ([docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/system/setup-e2e)).
- Do NOT blanket-apply `Modifier.safeDrawingPadding()` at root — that defeats edge-to-edge. Apply insets per-screen/per-component: `Modifier.windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)`, `imePadding()` on the composer, `navigationBarsPadding()` on bottom bars, `statusBarsPadding()` on top bars. Chat-specific: message list draws behind nav bar (scrim or transparent), composer sits above IME via `WindowInsets.ime`.
- 3-button nav still gets a translucent scrim automatically; gesture nav is fully transparent.

**Adaptive (phone/foldable/tablet).**
- `androidx.compose.material3.adaptive`: `ListDetailPaneScaffold` (conversation list → thread, the canonical chat pattern), `SupportingPaneScaffold`, `NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold` — these preserve state across form-factor changes (positional-memoization safe). Drive with `currentWindowAdaptiveInfo()` / `WindowSizeClass`.
- Foldables: `androidx.window` (`WindowInfoTracker`) for hinge/folding features; avoid putting the composer under a hinge — use `WindowInsetsRulers` / hinge-aware padding.
- Canonical guidance: [developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/build-adaptive-apps](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/build-adaptive-apps).

**Dynamic type.** Compose `sp` units follow system font scale automatically; test at 200% scale. Rules: never hardcode `dp` heights on text containers, use `Modifier.heightIn(min=)` + flexible layouts, don't cap `fontScale` (capping breaks accessibility audits), verify bubble widths with longest-locale strings (German) at max scale.

**Cyberpunk/neon dark theme tokens (concrete recipe).** Define two `ColorScheme`s and pass into `MaterialExpressiveTheme(colorScheme = ...)`:
- `background #05010F`, `surface #0B0620`, `surfaceContainer*` ramp on deep violet; `primary #00F0FF` (cyan neon), `secondary #B537F2` (magenta), `tertiary #39FF14` (acid green, sparing — timestamps, online dots); `error #FF2A6D`.
- Neon glow without custom draw code: `Modifier.shadow(elevation, spotColor = primary)` + `graphicsLayer` on expressive springs; or a `drawBehind` bloom for the send button. Keep `onPrimary/onSurface` at ≥4.5:1 — neon-on-black passes easily, neon-on-neon doesn't.
- Pair with `MotionScheme.expressive()` springs and an expressive `Shapes` (large rounded = 28dp+ bubbles) for the cyberpunk-soft look.

## 2. Chat UI libraries: native Compose vs cross-platform

**Native (recommended for this use case).**
| Need | Library | URL |
|---|---|---|
| Full chat UI (Compose) | Stream Chat Compose v7: `ChannelScreen`/`MessageList`/`MessageComposer`, `ChatTheme(componentFactory=…)` for customization | [getstream.io/chat/docs/sdk/android/compose/overview](https://getstream.io/chat/docs/sdk/android/compose/overview/) · [github.com/GetStream/stream-chat-android](https://github.com/GetStream/stream-chat-android) |
| Markdown incl. code blocks | mikepenz multiplatform-markdown-renderer (`-m3` module + `-code` module for Highlights-based syntax highlighting w/ language header + copy button) | [github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer) |
| Streaming (token-by-token) markdown | Same lib: `rememberStreamingMarkdownState()` + `append(chunk)`, or `Flow.collectAsStreamingMarkdownState()` — re-parses only the unstable tail | same repo, `Streaming` section of README (verified live) |
| Image attach/render | Coil 3 `AsyncImage` (`io.coil-kt.coil3:coil-compose:3.6.0`); markdown lib has `-coil3` transformer (`Coil3ImageTransformerImpl`) | [coil-kt.github.io/coil](https://coil-kt.github.io/coil/compose) |
| Camera capture | CameraX (`androidx.camera:camera-camera2/lifecycle/view`) + `ActivityResultContracts.TakePicture()`; gallery via Android 13+ Photo Picker (`PickVisualMedia`) — no storage permission needed | [developer.android.com/media/camera/camerax](https://developer.android.com/media/camera/camerax) |
| Voice input | Platform `SpeechRecognizer` / `RecognizerIntent.ACTION_RECOGNIZE_SPEECH` — no library needed; stream partial results into the composer | [developer.android.com/reference/android/speech/SpeechRecognizer](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/speech/SpeechRecognizer) |
| Voice *messages* (record/play) | Stream SDK has audio-recording guide; else `MediaRecorder` + `ExoPlayer`/`Media3` | [getstream.io XML voice-recording guide](https://getstream.io/chat/docs/sdk/android/ui/guides/enabling-audio-recording/) |
| Haptics | `LocalHapticFeedback.current.performHapticFeedback(HapticFeedbackType…)` — `LongPress`, `TextHandleMove`, `Confirm` on send, `Reject` on error | [developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/touch-input](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/touch-input) |

Notes: Stream is a hosted backend (self-hostable only at enterprise tier) — if the chat backend itself must be self-hosted, use Stream's UI components for reference only and pair the markdown/Coil/CameraX stack above with your own backend. The old `mikepenz/markdown-compose` repo name is dead (404) — the maintained artifact is `multiplatform-markdown-renderer`. Alternatives: [jeziellago/compose-markdown](https://github.com/jeziellago/compose-markdown), [feiyin0719/ComposeMarkdown](https://github.com/feiyin0719/ComposeMarkdown).

**Cross-platform.** [KevinnZou/compose-webview-multiplatform](https://github.com/KevinnZou/compose-webview-multiplatform) (WebView in shared Compose code, JS bridge `kmpJsBridge`), mikepenz renderer is KMP (Android/iOS/Desktop/Web from one call), Stream ships Flutter/React Native SDKs. Verdict: for an Android-first agent-observation app with CDP/VNC embedding, go native — the embedding APIs (WebView, foreground services, autofill) are all platform-specific anyway; share only the markdown renderer if iOS ever matters.

## 3. Self-hosted push without Firebase

Three-layer decision: **(a)** push *protocol* lib in-app, **(b)** always-on transport fallback, **(c)** exposure via Cloudflare.

**(a) Protocol options.**
| Option | What it is | Repos/docs |
|---|---|---|
| **UnifiedPush** (recommended) | Open protocol; app embeds `android-connector`, user picks a distributor (ntfy / Sunup / NextPush / Conversations). Server side speaks standard Web Push (RFC 8291 `aes128gcm` + optional VAPID RFC 8292). Encrypted, de-Googlable, works via F-Droid | [unifiedpush.org](https://unifiedpush.org) · [android-connector](https://github.com/UnifiedPush/android-connector) · [implementations](https://unifiedpush.org/developers/implementations/) · [intro](https://unifiedpush.org/developers/intro/) |
| **ntfy direct** | Self-host `ntfy` server, app subscribes per topic: `GET /topic/json` (NDJSON, recommended), `/topic/sse` (EventSource), `/topic/ws` (WebSocket). Built-in `since=` replay, `poll=1`, priorities, auth, attachments, keepalive events | [github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy](https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy) · [subscribe API](https://docs.ntfy.sh/subscribe/api/) · [self-host](https://docs.ntfy.sh/install/) |
| **Gotify direct** | Self-host `gotify/server` (Go, REST + WebSocket stream, web UI, plugins); official Android app reference for foreground-service pattern | [github.com/gotify/server](https://github.com/gotify/server) · [github.com/gotify/android](https://github.com/gotify/android) |

Recommendation: **UnifiedPush with ntfy-as-distributor** — one integration gets you both the user-choice story and ntfy's self-hosted server; fall back to embedded `embedded_fcm_distributor` only if you ever accept Play Services. Pure-ntfy-direct is simpler if you control both ends and don't need distributor choice.

**(b) Always-on transport (the hard part without FCM).** No push standard survives Doze/OEM killers by itself:
- Run a `foregroundServiceType="remoteMessaging"` (Android 14+) foreground service holding the ntfy SSE/WS or UnifiedPush distributor connection; ntfy sends `keepalive` events — use them as the connection health signal.
- You MUST route users through a battery-optimization exemption flow (`REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` intent) — Gotify documents exactly this plus `dontkillmyapp.com` per-OEM steps. Minimize the persistent notification via channel importance (Android 8+), as Gotify's README describes.
- Cache + replay server-side (`since=<last-id>`) so gaps from Doze windows backfill on reconnect.

**(c) Cloudflare Tunnel / Access tradeoffs.**
- **Tunnel** ([docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/)): `cloudflared` makes outbound-only connections — no inbound ports, no public IP. This is how your ntfy/Gotify/WebSocket origin is reachable. WebSockets are fully supported through tunnels.
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
- Watch idle timeouts on long-lived SSE through any proxy — prefer the `/ws` or `/json` endpoints with keepalives and client-side reconnect with backoff.

## 4. In-app browser embedding: WebView vs VNC vs CDP relay

For "observe the agent's browser" (your Playwright/Chrome-extension setup):

| Approach | Fit | Key facts |
|---|---|---|
| **WebView** | Best for *rendering pages inside the chat app* (login pages, agent-view snapshots) | `androidx.webkit`, JS bridge via `addJavascriptInterface` / `WebViewCompat`; Compose wrapper: [KevinnZou/compose-webview](https://github.com/KevinnZou/compose-webview) (Android) — Accompanist's web module is deprecated, don't build on it. Full DOM control, no pixels-over-wire. Cannot attach to an *external* Chrome. |
| **VNC client** | Only if the agent runs a full remote desktop | No maintained first-party Compose VNC widget; you'd embed [noVNC](https://github.com/novnc/noVNC) in a WebView (VNC→WebSocket→canvas). Heavy: full desktop encode, no DOM semantics, painful input mapping. Avoid unless the agent box is VNC-only. |
| **CDP relay (recommended)** | Best for *observing + driving an external agent Chrome* | Chrome on the box runs `--remote-debugging-port`; expose via Cloudflare Tunnel; app holds a WebSocket to `/json` and speaks CDP: `Page.startScreencast` for live MJPEG-ish observation, `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`/`dispatchKeyEvent` for control, `Runtime.evaluate` for Playwright-style queries. Transport with OkHttp WebSocket + kotlinx.serialization; optional JVM client [kklisura/chrome-devtools-java-client](https://github.com/kklisura/chrome-devtools-java-client). This mirrors your existing CDP-bridge architecture and keeps DOM-level control Playwright/extension flows need. |
