# 01 — Claude mobile app UX autopsy

Source of truth: grand-plan.md. This doc is research input, not decisions.
Researched 2026-10-03 from primary Anthropic sources (code.claude.com, support.claude.com, Play listing).

## 1. App structure

- Single "Claude" app (Play `com.anthropic.claude`, 50M+, 4.6). No separate Code app.
- Bottom nav: chat home + **Code tab**. `claude.ai/code/new` starts a Code session.
- Code tab → session list, `code` → Projects → New project.

## 2. Session list

- Sessions found by name at Code tab / `claude.ai/code`.
- Remote Control sessions: computer icon + green online dot.
- Title precedence: explicit `--name` → `/rename` → last meaningful message → auto `host-adjective-noun`.
- Paid plans: RAG search over past chats (surfaced as tool calls, citations link back).
  - Scope: all non-project chats together; inside a project only that project's chats.
  - Incognito (ghost icon) excluded from search/memory.

## 3. Chat + input bar

- `+` menu: Add files/photos, Memory off-switch (must be set BEFORE first message, locked after).
- Mic = dictation (speech→text, text reply). Sound-wave = full-duplex voice mode.
- Model menu next to send: model + effort + thinking. Changeable anytime, applies from next response.
- Effort: Low/Medium/High/xHigh (Opus long agentic)/Max. Thinking toggle with timer + expandable section.
- Newer models force thinking on.

## 4. Attachments pipeline

- Types: PDF/DOCX/CSV/TXT/HTML/ODT/RTF/EPUB/JSON/XLSX (XLSX needs code exec). Images JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP.
- Limits: 500MB/file, ≤20/chat, images ≤8000×8000, PDF ≤1000 pages (visual ≤100). Project files 30MB/file.
- Remote Control from phone: photos → visible to Claude + saved `~/.claude/uploads/`;
  other files → downloaded to host, passed as `@` refs; `@` autocompletes local project paths.
- Undownloadable → `[n of m attachments did not arrive]` note, message still delivered.

## 5. Voice

- Dictation: all plans, 12 languages (EN/FR/DE/HI/IT/JA/KO/PT/RU/ES/TR/UK, non-EN beta).
  Audio deleted after transcription, not used for training.
- Voice mode (beta, phone-first): hands-free (pause-detect) vs push-to-talk, voice+pace picker,
  model selector, mid-conversation code-switch, transcripts saved as text, connected tools usable.

## 6. Background / push / widget

- Phone never runs code. Cloud sessions survive phone close, persist across devices.
- Remote Control drives own machine (must stay awake, `tmux`/`screen`; sleep → auto-reconnect).
- Push triggers: Claude-initiated (task done, decision needed) or explicit ("notify me when…").
  Two `/config` toggles: `Push when Claude decides`, `Push when actions required`.
- Setup: same account/org, OS notify permission, open app once to refresh push token.
- Skipped while typing/focused; `CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE` extends presence suppression.
- Android battery optimization can delay push → app must guide exemption.
- Widget (Android 8.0+, resizable): spark = new chat, camera = new chat + camera,
  mic = new chat + dictation. All widget starts count toward usage.

## 7. Permission prompts

- Modes (dropdown by prompt box): cloud Accept-edits (default), Plan, Auto (org-gated).
  Self-started Remote Control: Manual, Accept edits, Plan — no Auto, no Bypass from app.
- Manual = approve edits/shell/network. acceptEdits = + file ops in scope.
  Plan = research only until plan approved. Auto = classifier reviews, ask-rules still prompt.
- Deny rules win everywhere. `rm` on critical paths, `AskUserQuestion`, org-`ask` connectors never auto-approved.
- Permission prompts + `AskUserQuestion` stay open until answered in-thread.
  Other dialogs expire after 5 min (`dialogExpiry`).
- Mobile command limits: `/plugin`, `/resume`, `/claude-api` are local-only.
  From app use arg-forms: `/model sonnet`, `/effort high`, `/compact`, `/context`, `/usage`, `/rename`, `/mcp`.

## 8. Projects vs chats

- Chats: single linear thread; optional incognito (unsaved) or memory-off (saved, unremembered).
- Classic Projects: workspace with own chats + knowledge + instructions + per-project memory.
  Paid RAG ~10× capacity. Search stays inside the project.
- New Projects beta (Code-first): coordinator conversation + parallel worker threads
  (own branch/PR each, auto-fix watching). Overview: Threads (Ready/Waiting/Working/Landing/Idle/Resolved),
  Library, Pull requests, Routines. `Work locally` runs one thread via Remote Control.
  Cap 200 new threads/day; idle costs nothing; Delete is permanent.
- Mobile creation: Code tab → Projects → New project (Name required, Goal + Context optional).

## 9. OS citizenship (why the bar is high)

- Android intents/share/clock/calendar/maps/Health Connect with native charts.
- Contextual least-privilege prompts with preview-before-send (Messages/Email need no perm via share+preview).
- Per-topic memory with edit/delete, per-chat kill switch, incognito, never-save IDs.
- Enterprise: SSO/SCIM, model allowlists, Trusted Devices (biometric/passkey step-up), audit logs.

## 10. Takeaways for opencode remote

- Copy: Code-tab session list with online dots, `+` attach menu, memory pre-first-message switch,
  model+effort picker by send button, presence-aware push, resizable 3-button widget,
  in-thread approvals that never silently expire, per-project memory scoping.
- Beat: opencode sessions run on OUR hardware (no cloud), so push needs our own bridge;
  permission model maps to opencode allow/ask/deny + remember — simpler, show it inline like Claude's cards.

## Sources

- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mobile
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-projects
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes
- https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.anthropic.claude
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10534883-use-the-claude-widget-on-android
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11869629-use-claude-with-android-apps
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11101966-use-voice-mode
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065434-use-dictation-on-claude-mobile
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-upload-files-to-claude
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context
- https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects

# 02 — AI mobile app patterns (ChatGPT / Gemini / generic)

Source of truth: grand-plan.md. Research input, not decisions.
Covers the "ai mobile app" brief item: what good AI apps share, beyond Claude specifics.

## 1. Universal chat-app skeleton

- Three-pane information architecture: sidebar/session drawer → thread → composer.
  Mobile collapses to one pane with bottom-sheet drawer + back-stack navigation.
- Session list rows: title + timestamp + status dot (idle/working/error). Search field pinned at top.
- Composer anatomy (left→right): `+` attach → text field (multiline, grows to ~5 lines) →
  mic → send/stop morphing button. Model/ratio chip above or beside send.
- Streaming: tokens append in place; stop button replaces send while busy; auto-scroll
  with "jump to latest" FAB when user scrolls up (see grapeot PRD: 60% of time is reading).

## 2. Message rendering rules

- Markdown first-class: headings, lists, tables, code fences with language header + copy button,
  inline code chips, links as tappable spans. Render incrementally (streaming tail re-parse only).
- Tool/activity cards: collapsible rows per tool call (pending → running → done/error),
  expandable diff/patch views, todo checklists with live check-off.
- Reasoning blocks: collapsed by default with timer ("thought for 12s"), expandable.
- Cost/token footer per turn: small muted line (input/output/cached tokens + $) — matches H10 stats.
- Error states render INLINE (model failure inside 200 response): red card with retry button,
  never a toast-only failure.

## 3. Sessions lifecycle patterns

- New chat is instant (no modal); title backfills from first exchange. Explicit rename via long-press.
- Fork/branch: long-press a message → "branch from here". Archive vs delete separated
  (archive hides, delete destroys + confirms).
- Cross-device continuity: server is source of truth; client reconciles on foreground
  (status poll + message fetch). Optimistic send with rollback on failure.
- Temporary/incognito: one toggle at creation; temp chats excluded from search/history/export.

## 4. Input modalities

- Dictation (speech→text into composer) vs voice mode (full duplex conversation) — offer both,
  like Claude. Dictation is cheap (platform SpeechRecognizer); voice mode is a workstream.
- Attach: photo picker (no storage perm), camera (CameraX), file picker (SAF, scoped).
  Show staged attachments as chips above composer with remove ×; compress images by setting.
- Slash commands: `/` in composer opens autocomplete sheet over keyboard; custom commands listed with descriptions.

## 5. Notifications done right

- Reply notifications: HIGH channel, direct-reply action + mark-read action.
- Approval stalls: separate channel, approve/deny inline actions on the notification itself.
- Quiet hours setting + per-session mute. Never badge the launcher for agent-typing noise.
- Presence-awareness: suppress push for the session currently open on screen.

## 6. Anti-patterns seen in wrapper apps

- Fire-and-forget bubbles with no tool visibility (user can't see what agent did).
- Blocking HTTP send with spinner (dies on radio drop; use async + SSE).
- Hidden history / no export / no delete (trust killer).
- Blanket permission grabs at install (storage+contacts for a chat app).
- WebView-wrapped website shipped as "app" (no offline, no push, no widget, slow).
- No empty states, no offline states, no retry affordance — just spinners.

## 7. Takeaways for opencode remote

- Skeleton: drawer list + thread + composer is non-negotiable; add agent/model chips (opencode-specific).
- Inline tool cards + reasoning collapse + per-turn cost footer = the quality bar.
- Async send + reconcile is the ONLY send path for long turns (matches S3/H1).
- Temp mode, per-session mute, quiet hours all ship (F5 settings).

# 03 — Third-party opencode clients (incl. R11 teardown targets)

Source of truth: grand-plan.md. Research input, not decisions.
Researched 2026-10-03 via gh_grep + repo README/RFC fetches.

- Repo: https://github.com/alvarolorentedev/opencode-mobile — Apache-2.0, 232★/25 forks

- Stack: React Native + Expo (~57) + TS + Expo Router, react-native-paper,
  `@opencode-ai/sdk` + `@opencode/client`, expo-secure-store, expo-notifications, Playwright web e2e.

# 04 — Mobile development principles & philosophy (good / bad practices)

Source of truth: grand-plan.md. Applies to all implementation phases.

## 1. Guiding principles

- Server is source of truth; phone is a smart cache. Every screen must survive process death
  (ViewModel + SavedStateHandle + Room), because Android WILL kill the process.
- Async-first: no blocking network on main thread, no synchronous send-then-spinner.
  Every request has timeout + retry + visible state (sending/sent/failed-retry).
- Offline is a state, not an error: cached sessions/threads render read-only with a banner;
  queued sends flush on reconnect. Design empty/offline/error states before happy path.
- Least privilege, most clarity: each permission requested with a sentence saying WHY;
  aggressive onboarding (per user decision) lists all, but each row still explains itself.
- Battery is a feature: no polling loops; SSE only while foreground (or bounded FGS);
  WorkManager for deferred work; respect Doze instead of fighting it (see doc 05).

## 2. Architecture hygiene (Android)

- MVVM + UDF: `ViewModel` holds `StateFlow<UiState>`; Composables render, never fetch.
- Layering: `:app` (wiring) → `:feature:*` (screens+VMs) → `:domain` (pure Kotlin use-cases, no Android imports)
  → `:data` (Retrofit/Room/DataStore/WorkManager behind interfaces). KMP-extractable later.
- Repository interfaces in `:domain`, implementations in `:data`. Push behind `PushGateway`
  interface (UnifiedPush / FGS-fallback). Theme behind `ThemeRepository` (JSON tokens → M3 scheme).
- One source of truth per datum: sessions list from one Flow; thread from one Flow;
  never two caches of the same session diverging.
- Dependency injection with Hilt; no service locators, no static singletons holding Context.

## 3. Networking discipline (the S3 connection contract in code)

- OkHttp single client: preemptive Basic auth + 401 Authenticator, TLS (no cleartext off-device),
  `network_security_config.xml` allowlist (localhost/`10.0.2.2` only for dev).
- `prompt_async` for sends (204, no long-lived HTTP). Sync `POST message` only for short turns w/ timeout.
- SSE: one EventSource to `/event` (fallback `/global/event`), 1s→30s exp backoff + jitter,
  `since=`/status-poll resync after reconnect. `?directory=` on every request.
- Version pin: `GET /global/health` at connect; gate behavior per server version; defensive-parse
  unknown event/part fields (log + skip, never crash).
- Structured concurrency: `viewModelScope` + `SupervisorJob`; cancel streams on `onCleared`;
  no `GlobalScope`, no leaked callbacks.

## 4. Compose rules

- State hoisting: screens stateless, state lives in VM. `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`.
- Lazy lists with stable keys; `key(session.id)` everywhere; avoid re-composition storms
  during streaming (buffer deltas ~100–200ms before recompose of markdown tail).
- Streaming markdown: `rememberStreamingMarkdownState` + append; re-parse tail only.
- Insets per-component (`imePadding`, `navigationBarsPadding`, `statusBarsPadding`);
  never root-level `safeDrawingPadding`. IME-animated composer (see doc 08).
- Test at 200% font scale + German-length strings; no hardcoded dp heights on text containers.

## 5. Good practices checklist

- Baseline Profiles + R8 + App Bundle from P0; measure startup (TTID) on an API-26 device.
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
  no secrets in logs, no PII in crash reports.
- Notification channels from day one (HIGH replies, LOW status); never reuse/delete channels.
- Feature flags / settings for every behavior (F5 catalog, doc 13) — but flags need owners + defaults.
- Tests: ViewModel + repository unit tests; fake `serve` (see alvarolorentedev `tests/*.test.mjs` pattern,
  port to MockWebServer); screenshot tests for theme tokens; manual Doze/OEM matrix (doc 05 §6).

## 6. Bad practices (banned)

- Blocking REST for agent turns; perpetual background SSE; polling the server on a timer.
- `GlobalScope`, static Context, leaking EventSources across config changes.
- Hardcoded colors/sp/dp (all through theme tokens, doc 08/13).
- Blind `PATCH /config` (GET-then-merge only); blind schema assumptions (defensive parse).
- WebView-wrapped site as "app"; Expo-style JS push infra (we are on-prem, doc 09).
- Compressing plans, skipping verification, drifting from grand-plan (project rule, not just code).

# 05 — Android constraints 2025–2026 (background, battery, insets, minSdk)

Source of truth: grand-plan.md. Verified 2026-10-03 against official Android docs.
Re-verify Play target-SDK deadline + FGS-notification-without-grant rendering at build time.

## 1. Headline: no perpetual background SSE

Five releases made indefinite background sockets impractical: bg FGS-start bans (12+),
mandatory FGS types (14+), `dataSync` 6h/24h cap (15+), job quotas alongside FGS (16),
Doze deferral, OEM killers. Supported architecture: **push-to-wake + short-lived connections**
(open SSE only while chat UI foreground or bounded sync). Our push = ntfy bridge (doc 09).

## 2. Foreground service types (mandatory API 34+)

- Every FGS declares `android:foregroundServiceType` + holds `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + type permission.
- `dataSync`: uploads/downloads/fetch — closest fit for agent sync, subject to 6h cap.
- `remoteMessaging`: device-to-device SMS-style relay ONLY — claiming it for agent SSE risks Play rejection.
- `specialUse`: needs manifest justification + Play Console declaration + human review.
- `shortService` (34+): ~3-min timeout, no sticky — "finish send after backgrounding" only.
- What we use: `dataSync` FGS started from visible activity for live SSE while chatting;
  stop on backgrounding. UIDT jobs (34+, `RUN_USER_INITIATED_JOBS`) for attachment uploads;
  FGS-worker fallback below 34.
- Background start ban (31+): no `startForegroundService()` from background
  (`ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`). Exemptions: high-priority FCM (n/a — no Firebase),
  user tap on notification/widget, battery-optimizations-off, visible overlay.
- Boot (targetSdk 35+): boot receiver CANNOT launch `dataSync`/camera/mic FGS — schedule WorkManager instead.
- `dataSync` 6h/24h cap: overrun → `onTimeout()` then crash if not stopped in seconds;
  exhausted quota at start → start exception. Honor via timeout + WorkManager handoff.
- Android 16: jobs running concurrently with an FGS count against JobScheduler quota.
  Monitor `WorkInfo.getStopReason()` / `JobParameters.getStopReason()`.

## 3. Doze / App Standby / battery exemption

- Doze (screen off, stationary, unplugged): network suspended, jobs/alarms deferred to
  shrinking maintenance windows. App Standby: untouched apps → network ~1×/day until charger.
- Official line: use push infra (FCM in docs; ntfy+UnifiedPush in our case), not own socket.
- Exemption flow: `PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations()` → settings intent
  (`ACTION_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATION_SETTINGS`) preferred; direct request
  (`ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS`) is Play-restricted for chat apps —
  USER CHOSE fully-aggressive anyway: we do the direct request, accept Play-review risk,
  sideload first / Play later. Recorded as decision D5.
- OEM killers (dontkillmyapp.com, re-verified 2026-06), worst→least:
  Huawei > Xiaomi > OnePlus > Samsung > rest; Pixel ≈ stock.
  - Samsung: sleeping/deep-sleeping lists + auto re-sleep (~3 days); needs Don't-optimize + Recents lock.
    One UI 6.0+: FGS of API-34-targeted apps "work as intended".
  - Xiaomi/MIUI: Autostart permission + Battery saver → No restrictions + Recents pin required by default.
    Detect autostart state via community MIUI-autostart API.
- Budget: in-app "background health" screen (P4) — exemption status, OEM deep-link instructions,
  ntfy registration diagnostics. No code path survives Xiaomi/Samsung defaults without user action.

## 4. Notifications

- `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` runtime permission since API 33 — request in aggressive onboarding with rationale.
- Channels (API 26+): create BEFORE posting; importance user-overridable → choose deliberately:
  agent-reply HIGH, approval-stall HIGH (separate channel), FGS-status LOW/MIN, no sound.
  Never delete/recreate channels (resets user prefs).
- FGS still needs a `Notification` object regardless of grant — honest "connection live" indicator.
- API 34+: full-screen intent needs `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT` + user grant (reserve for calls, not messages).
  Don't rely on exact alarms for keepalive (`SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` is user-granted).

## 5. Edge-to-edge (forced on targetSdk 35+ / Android 15)

- Status/nav transparent, offsets disabled; `setStatusBarColor`/`setDecorFitsSystemWindows` deprecated.
- Cutout modes coerced to ALWAYS — pad around `WindowInsets.displayCutout` yourself.
- Implementation: `enableEdgeToEdge()` + per-component insets (Views: `ViewCompat` listener;
  Compose: `statusBars`/`navigationBars`/`displayCutout`/`ime` insets, Scaffold `contentWindowInsets`).
- Material3 Compose handles insets mostly automatically; Material2 does NOT.
- Chat-critical: composer padding driven by ANIMATED IME inset, not `adjustResize` alone;
  test gesture nav + 3-button nav + cutout/foldable images. Audit onboarding/settings screens too.

## 6. minSdk / targetSdk — LOCKED: minSdk 26, targetSdk current

- minSdk 26 (Android 8.0, 2017): channels native, Autofill, adaptive icons, ShortcutManager,
  uniform background-limits baseline. Drops ~7.x (small, shrinking — confirm in Play Console stats).
- Desugaring (`coreLibraryDesugaringEnabled`) backports `java.time`/streams/concurrent to the 20s —
  language APIs are NOT a reason to raise minSdk; only framework behaviors are.
- Compose + M3 + Room + WorkManager + DataStore all support 21+ — no constraint from minSdk 26.
- targetSdk/compileSdk track current Play requirement independently (35 required Aug 2025;
  36 enforcement on August cadence — verify at build time).
- Device lab for P6 hardening: physical or imaged API 26 (channels/FGS-old), API 33 (notif perm),
  API 35 (edge-to-edge forced), Samsung + Xiaomi skins, foldable.

| Background services | Full FGS/WorkManager/Doze control | Same Android, zero iOS share | Isolates plumbing, second-class | Deprecated bg-fetch → bg-task, weakest |
| Startup | Fastest (baseline profiles, R8) | Same | Engine-init cost | Slowest (Hermes helps, still bundle parse) |
| APK size | Smallest (R8, bundles, ABI splits) | Slightly larger | Largest (libflutter.so per ABI) | Mid-large |
| Chat/SSE/markdown | OkHttp EventSource + streaming markdown, full control | Transport shared, UI per-platform anyway | Streaming jank + highlight gaps | Polyfill SSE, thinnest VNC |
| VNC + WebRTC | Google WebRTC SDK + JVM VNC, direct interop | Same Android, doubled iOS work | flutter-webrtc 701 open issues, VNC DIY | Community only, heavy bridging |
| Offline | Reference path (Room+DataStore+WM) | Feasible (KMP samples) | Two failure domains | Weakest scheduling |
| Theming | M3 dynamic color, CompositionLocal tokens | Same Android, iOS separate anyway | M3 fidelity lags | Native views escape system |
| No-Firebase push | Best UnifiedPush host (Tusky/Element/Nextcloud Talk pattern) | Same Android | Needs native bridge | Same + worse scheduling |
| Staffing | Any Android hire productive | Needs Kotlin+Swift senior | Easy Dart hire, escapes need Kotlin anyway | Largest pool, heaviest churn |

# 09 — Push without Firebase (ntfy + UnifiedPush + bridge)

Source of truth: grand-plan.md. No Firebase, no paid services — on-prem only.
Topology: `ntfy.uchabokeria.space` (doc: grand-plan §Topology).

## 1. Why a bridge is required

Android cannot hold a perpetual background SSE (doc 05): Doze, 6h `dataSync` cap,
OEM killers. When the app is dead, SOMETHING server-side must observe `serve` and wake the phone.
That something = tiny self-hosted bridge on blackwall: watches `serve /event` SSE,
publishes to self-hosted ntfy topics. Phone subscribes via UnifiedPush (ntfy distributor).

## 2. Components

- **ntfy server** (self-hosted, Go, single binary): topics over HTTPS;
  `GET /topic/json` (NDJSON + `since=` replay — use this), `/topic/sse`, `/topic/ws`;
  priorities, auth, attachments, keepalive events. https://docs.ntfy.sh · https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy
- **Bridge** (`serve → ntfy`, custom, runs on blackwall next to `serve`):
  opens `GET /event` SSE with Basic auth; on `message.part.updated` (reply done → `session.idle`),
  `permission.updated` (approval stall), `session.error` → POST to ntfy topic with priority +
  minimal payload (session id + title + snippet; never secrets).
  Supervised (systemd unit, auto-restart = "resurrection" on server side); backoff reconnect;
  dedupe by event id; `since=` gap backfill on its own reconnect.
- **App (UnifiedPush)**: embed `android-connector`; user picks distributor (ntfy app / Sunup / NextPush).
  https://unifiedpush.org · https://github.com/UnifiedPush/android-connector
- **Fallback (no distributor installed)**: foreground `dataSync` service holding ntfy SSE/WS
  directly + battery-exemption UX (Gotify android pattern); degraded, documented as such.

## 3. Topic + auth design (OPEN — spec phase with user)

- One topic per user-device or per server? Proposal: `opencode-<user>-<device>` unguessable names
  (random suffix), ntfy-native auth (Basic/token) stored in EncryptedSharedPreferences.
- Machine endpoints stay OFF Cloudflare Access (Access breaks machine clients);
  protected by ntfy auth + unguessable topics. Access only on human web UI, if ever.
- Payloads: session id, event type, short snippet. Full content pulled via `serve` API on tap
  (payload minimization = privacy + Doze-friendly small pushes).

## 4. Notification mapping (app side)

- Reply done → HIGH channel, actions: Open / Direct-reply / Mark-read. Presence-aware:
  suppress for session currently open on screen.
- Approval stall (`permission.updated`, `AskUserQuestion`) → separate HIGH channel,
  inline Approve / Deny actions on the notification itself.
- Bridge/error events → LOW channel (status), no sound.
- Quiet hours + per-session mute (settings) applied client-side before posting.

## 5. Cloudflare Tunnel notes

- `cloudflared` outbound-only; no inbound ports. WebSockets fully supported through tunnels.
- Prefer `/json` (NDJSON) or `/ws` endpoints with keepalives + client backoff over bare SSE
  through proxies (idle timeouts). Use ntfy keepalive events as connection-health signal.
- Cache + replay server-side (`since=<last-id>`) so Doze gaps backfill.

## 6. What we do NOT use

- FCM (Google dependency — banned by brief). Expo push (third-party cloud — banned).
- `remoteMessaging` FGS type for this (Play-policy risk, doc 05).

Source of truth: grand-plan.md. Lint- and review-enforced.

## 1. Connection code (S3 contract)

- Single OkHttpClient (timeouts from settings); preemptive Basic + 401 Authenticator;
  TLS only off-device; `network_security_config.xml` dev allowlist.
- Repository per aggregate (`SessionRepository`, `MessageRepository`, …) behind `:domain` interfaces.
- SSE manager: one EventSource lifecycle owner; backoff 1s→30s + jitter; resync via
  `/session/status` + `GET message?limit=`; `?directory=` always; version pin from `/global/health`.
- Defensive parsing: unknown event/part fields → log + skip, never crash. Contract tests against
  recorded `/doc` fixtures per server version.
- No `GlobalScope`; `viewModelScope`/`SupervisorJob`; cancel on `onCleared`.
- Never spawn `serve` from the app; never call `/instance/dispose`; never blind `PATCH /config`.

## 2. Session/message handling

- `prompt_async` sends; reconcile on `session.idle`; optimistic message with rollback.
- Deltas appended, never replaced; buffer ~100–200ms before recompose.
- Model errors inside 200s render inline with retry (never toast-only).
- Temp sessions filtered client-side (D2: hide locally); purge action + auto-purge setting.
- Client-side Projects entity (D1) → dirs; memory/instructions injected as system context on send.

## 3. Android hygiene

- Hilt DI; no statics holding Context; `SavedStateHandle` for process-death survival.
- Secrets: EncryptedSharedPreferences + Keystore; no secrets in logs/crash reports.
- `FLAG_SECURE` on browser-observation + optional whole-app (setting).
- Channels created once at install; WorkManager unique work names; FGS started only from visible activity.
- Tests: VM + repo unit tests, MockWebServer fake-serve, theme screenshot tests,
  manual Doze/OEM/device-lab matrix (doc 05 §6).

# 12 — App optimization & techniques

Source of truth: grand-plan.md.

## 1. Startup

- Baseline Profiles (compose + navigation paths) from P0; measure TTID on API-26 device.
- Lazy-init: don't open SSE, don't load providers/agents/commands until server connected.
- Hilt + R8 + App Bundle + per-ABI splits; keep `:app` wiring thin.

## 2. List + render perf

- LazyColumn stable `key(id)`; streaming buffer ~100–200ms; tail-only markdown re-parse
  (`rememberStreamingMarkdownState`); Coil async images with size bounds; diff/patch collapsed default.
- Avoid recomposition storms: hoist streaming state, use `derivedStateOf` for scroll-derived UI
  (jump-to-latest FAB, date dividers).

## 3. Network efficiency

- `prompt_async` + SSE deltas (no polling loops); status-poll ONLY as SSE-drop fallback with backoff.
- `GET message?limit=` paging; don't refetch full threads on every foreground (ETag/reconcile by `time.updated`).
- Image attach compressed client-side before staging (setting); camera capture resolution capped (setting).

## 4. Battery

- SSE socket lifetime = chat screen visible (+ bounded FGS). Nothing periodic under 15 min;
  WorkManager unique periodic ≥15min for widget status + health checks.
- ntfy keepalives as health signal; `since=` backfill instead of re-pull storms.
- Respect Doze: schedule, don't fight. Exemption is user-granted (D5), never assumed.

## 5. Size

- R8 full mode, resource shrinking, no unused deps; WebRTC/CDP libs loaded per-feature module
  (dynamic-feature or on-demand) so base APK stays lean for non-browser users.

**Permission approve/deny state machine** (`src/bot/callbacks/permission-callback-handler.ts`):
- Callback `permission:<once|always|reject>`. Guards: manager active → active message ID → non-empty requestIDs, else `permission.inactive_callback` alert.

- Outcomes: accepted / gone (`PermissionNotFoundError` → settled outside) / failed. Failed → prompt stays answerable + delivery warning, re-tap resends. Success → `endPrompt(replied)` → buttons stripped, terminal line records tapped vs outside vs `⏹ Not answered` (abort/detach/stop/restart/run-end). Reconnect re-shows one prompt per distinct pending request (identical grouped).

**Question handling** (`src/bot/callbacks/question-callback-handler.ts`):
- Callback `question:<select|submit|custom|toggle_custom|cancel>:<qIdx>[:opt]`. Single-select answers immediately and advances (`showNextQuestion`); multi-select toggles + re-renders, Done submits via `question.reply` (V2 sends value, shows label). Custom button only when allowed; typed text requires Custom first; multi-select custom becomes extra tickable row.
- Cancel → `question.reject` → `❌ Poll cancelled`, turn ends with no reply/footer. Last question stays until OpenCode takes answers, then summary. Undelivered → warning, stays answerable. Externally settled → buttons removed + line. Serialization: one slot, FIFO; same-session new question replaces poll, subagent question from another session waits; `/abort|/detach|/opencode_stop` drops waiting. Active flow blocks unrelated input (hint); allowed: `/help /status /abort /detach /opencode_stop`. Subagent questions render like main agent's.

**Queue-vs-steer** (`src/bot/handlers/prompt-queue-dispatch.ts`, `/settings`):
- Modes: Off | On (V1) | Queue|Steer (V2, default Steer). Cap `MAX_QUEUED_PROMPTS=5`; waiting items = bottom-keyboard buttons, tap to withdraw.
- V2: busy prompts go straight to session inbox, bot holds nothing (no media cap). Steer = picked up mid-turn, same progress message + one footer; Queue = own run after. Restart kills buttons but OpenCode still delivers; reconnect reconciles (delivered → no button/quote, still-waiting → button + later quote).
- V1: bot holds queue, dispatches one-by-one on idle with `dispatchInFlight` guard, echoes as external-user-input quote. 20 MiB raw `file_size` media cap pre-download; unsized media refused while busy.
- `/detach` hands waiting items to detached session (agent/model frozen at detach, incl. transcribing/downloading); they leave keyboard + cap; later switch leaves them; `/abort` there or `/opencode_stop` withdraws. Pickup while detached → background notification only.

## 1. grapeot/opencode_android_client (NATIVE BLUEPRINT — copy patterns)

Repo: https://github.com/grapeot/opencode_android_client (branch `master`, MIT, 97★)

### Files to study first

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `app/.../data/api/OpenCodeApi.kt` | Full Retrofit interface (table below) |
| `app/.../data/api/SSEClient.kt` | OkHttp EventSource + infinite 1s→30s backoff + resync hooks |
| `app/.../data/repository/OpenCodeRepository.kt` | Dual-client (REST 60s / SSE infinite), Basic auth, `configure()` rebuild, optimistic send + `session.error` recovery |
| `app/.../ui/MainViewModel.kt` + `MainViewModelSyncActions.kt` | Single `StateFlow<AppState>`, `streamingPartTexts["msg:part"]` anti-flash, 20s SSE watchdog → REST reconcile |
| `app/.../data/model/SSE.kt`, `Permission.kt`, `Question.kt` | Event/part/permission/question models |
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
| `app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml` | `cleartext=false`, HTTP allowlist localhost/`10.0.2.2`/ts.net |
| `app/src/test/.../OpenCodeRepositoryTest.kt:298` | Test contract: `prompt_async` + Basic header + body shape |

### Endpoint table (verified against our live `/doc` — all exist on v1)

`GET global/health` · `GET session?limit=` · `POST session {title?,parentID?}` ·
`GET/PATCH/DELETE session/{id}` · `GET session/status` · `GET session/{id}/message?limit=` ·
`POST session/{id}/prompt_async {messageID?,parts[],agent="build",model?}` → 204 ·
`POST …/abort` · `POST …/fork {messageID?}` · `POST …/revert {messageID,partID?}` ·
`POST session/{id}/permissions/{pid} {response: once|always|reject}` ·
`GET /permission` + `POST /permission/{id}/reply {reply}` (PREFER — no session id; field is `reply`) ·
`GET /question` + `POST /question/{id}/reply {answers: string[][]}` + `POST …/reject` ·
`GET config/providers` (+ `GET /provider` fallback) · `GET /agent` · `GET …/diff` · `GET …/todo` ·
`GET /file?path=` · `GET /file/content?path=` (base64 images) · `GET /file/status` ·
`GET /find/file?query&limit=50`.

### JSON rules (copy verbatim)

`ignoreUnknownKeys + lenient + coerceInputValues`, `explicitNulls=false` (server rejects `model:null`),
`encodeDefaults=true` (keeps part `type` discriminator).

### SSE recipe (copy, then extend with FGS + ntfy)

- `GET {base}/global/event`, `Accept: text/event-stream`, manual Basic header.
- `retryWhen`: `delay((1000*2^attempt).coerceAtMost(30000))`, infinite.
- Skip blank/`[DONE]`; malformed frames skipped silently; `onClosed/onFailure` feed retry.
- Watchdog: server 10s heartbeat; no frame >20s → one REST reconcile (messages only if not busy).
- `message.part.delta` → append to `streamingPartTexts["$msg:$part"]` seeded from existing part text.
- `session.error` → drop optimistic rows, return text to composer, inline error.

### State model (adapt, don't clone)

Single `AppState` + derived slices; `visibleMessages` filters post-revert;
`attentionSessionIds = permission.sessionIds + question.sessionIds`;
per-session draft + model/agent memory; `contextUsage` from last assistant tokens vs provider limit;
`sessionStats` rolls up `parentID` subtree. Permission card: 3-button REJECT/ONCE/ALWAYS.
Deep links `opencode://session/<id>` (copy). NFC quick-prompt (skip).

### Explicit gaps THEY document (WE fill)

No background SSE, no FGS, no push — background disconnects, foreground full-syncs.
`question`/permission stalls with no push = "async idle" gap → our P4 (doc 09) exists because of this.
Voice needs external AI Builder → we use platform SpeechRecognizer (doc 08).

## 2. alvarolorentedev/opencode-mobile (UX + ONBOARDING — inspiration only, no code)

Repo: https://github.com/alvarolorentedev/opencode-mobile (Apache-2.0, 232★) · Docs: https://getopencode.app/docs/

- Onboarding: Welcome → Connect → Workspace → Preferences → Permissions → Ready;

- Connection profiles: `{id, name, serverUrl, username, modelPreferences{…}}`;
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
- Tunnel docs worth mirroring in our setup guide: LAN vs Tailscale vs Cloudflare Tunnel (named, auth mandatory,
  SSE/WebSocket must pass) vs reverse-proxy `/api` prefix vs SSH. Troubleshooting table
  (HTML/404 → wrong base; 401/403 → creds; SSE stall → proxy dropped streaming) → adapt to Tunnel-only.
- Permission cards: operation + pattern/path, Allow once / Always / Deny; prefer Allow-once guidance for
  destructive/network. Question cards: single/multi/custom, in-order, Reject ends turn.
- Usage sheet: context %, in/out/reasoning tokens, cache r/w, steps, cost ONLY with server pricing;
  "Pricing unavailable" ≠ free. Copy the copy.
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]

## 3. grinev/opencode-telegram-bot (STATE MACHINES — read before P2 ViewModels)

Repo: https://github.com/grinev/opencode-telegram-bot (MIT, 1.2k★)

- Permissions (`permission-callback-handler.ts`): guards (manager→message→non-empty IDs);
  `PermissionNotFoundError` = settled elsewhere; failed → stays answerable + warning, re-tap resends;
  success → buttons stripped + terminal line records outcome; reconnect re-shows one prompt per pending request.
- Questions (`question-callback-handler.ts`): single-select answers+advances; multi toggles + Done;
  custom only when allowed; cancel → `question.reject` ends turn; last question stays until consumed;
  one slot FIFO; same-session replaces, subagent-from-other-session waits.
- Queue-vs-steer (`prompt-queue-dispatch.ts`): Steer (mid-turn pickup) vs Queue (own run after), cap 5;
  V2 busy → session inbox, bot holds nothing; restart/reconnect reconciliation rules.
- Revert/fork (`message-history-callback-handler.ts`): user-message list newest-first paginated;
  revert rolls back + discards later; fork branches + sets current + applies agent/model/variant.
- Model picker (`model-selection-callback-handler.ts`): favorites → recents deduped, current ✅,
  stale tap redraws, variant picker iff >1 variant, agent pick applies its model silently.

## Proposed defaults (opencode permission types → default action)

| Type | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `edit` (in-scope files) | ALLOW (remember) | Core agent loop; Claude parity (acceptEdits) |
| `read`, `glob`, `grep` | ALLOW (remember) | Read-only, zero risk |
| `bash` (safe read-only: ls, git status/diff/log, cat…) | ALLOW (remember) | Triage speed; still logged |
| `bash` (mutating: rm -rf, chmod, curl \| sh, sudo…) | ASK always | Destructive / exfiltration surface |
| `webfetch` | ALLOW (remember, websearch default-on H3) | Matches H3 default |
| `task`, `skill` (non-destructive) | ALLOW (remember) | Subagent delegation is normal work |
| `external_directory` (outside session dir) | ASK always | Sandbox escape |
| `doom_loop` | ASK always | Runaway-loop guard |
| `question` (AskUserQuestion) | ASK always (cards, never auto) | Needs human judgment by definition |
| `skill` (destructive/unknown) | ASK always | Unknown side effects |

## Rules

- Deny rules (server config) override everything, always.
- "Remember" (`always`) scoped per session by default; global-always requires explicit toggle (setting).
[CREDENTIAL-RELATED LINE OMITTED]
- Server `--auto` mode surfaced in UI banner (asks bypassed server-side except denys).
- Failed reply (e.g. `PermissionNotFoundError` = settled elsewhere) → card refreshes, stays answerable (grinev rule).

# SPEC — P1 sessions + chat + streaming

Source of truth: `docs/grand-plan.md` §7. Implements: C1 (list/search/open incl. PC-created),
C2 (new + temp D2 + default-temp), C3 subset (rename/delete/abort; fork/revert/share/summarize/diff/todo
UI in P2, endpoints already declared), H1 (chat + streaming deltas), S3 hardened (SSE per doc 14 §1).

## 1. New module: `:feature-chat` (sessions list + thread + composer)

```
feature-chat/
  SessionsViewModel  (list/search/active, new+temp, rename/delete, status map)
  SessionsScreen     (search field, rows: title/time/status-dot/temp-badge, FAB new, long-press menu)
  ChatViewModel      (thread Flow, streamingPartTexts, send via prompt_async, abort, reconcile)
  ChatScreen         (MessageList + Composer; tool cards + reasoning collapse PLAIN in P1,
                      markdown lib lands in P2 — render text/code fences monospace for now)
  ChatNav            (route "chat/{sessionId}")
```

AppNav gains: Sessions tab (list) + `chat/{id}` route. Bottom nav: Servers / Sessions / Settings.

## 2. Data layer additions (`:data`, doc 14 copy-checklist)

- `SSEClient`: OkHttp EventSource → `{base}/global/event`, Basic header, infinite 1s→30s backoff+jitter,
  skip blank/`[DONE]`, `ignoreUnknownKeys` decode to `SSEEvent(directory?, type, payload)`,
  `server.heartbeat` noop. Lifecycle: `connect(profile)` returns `Flow<Result<SSEEvent>>`; cancel on scope end.
- `SessionRepository` (+ `:domain` interface): sessions Flow per active profile,
  `refresh()`, `create(title?, temp)`, `rename`, `delete`, `abort`, `statusMap`,
  `messages(id, limit)`, `sendPrompt(id, parts, agent, model, noReply)`.
- Temp (D2): `tempSessionIds` in DataStore (per profile); temp badge; list filter toggle
  "show temp"; purge action (delete all temp). NO server auto-delete.
- Reconcile: `session.status` event → if current && !busy: clear streaming overlays + refresh messages;
  `message.part.delta` → append `streamingPartTexts["msg:part"]`; `session.error` → drop optimistic,
  return text to composer, inline error card; 20s watchdog → one REST reconcile (grapeot rules).
- Models: `MessageWithParts(info, parts)`, `Part` sealed (text/reasoning/tool/step-start/step-finish/
  file/patch/agent/retry/compaction/subtask/unknown), `SessionStatusDto` extended
  (`type: idle|busy|retry`, retry{attempt,message}?) — defensive: unknown → `unknown` object, never crash.

## 3. UI rules (docs 02, 08)

- Rows: title + relative time + status dot (idle grey/working cyan/error red) + temp badge (magenta).
- Thread: user right / agent left; per-turn cost footer (from `step-finish{cost,tokens}`, muted small);
  error cards inline with Retry; "jump to latest" FAB; pull-to-refresh → status-poll resync.
- Composer: text field (grows ≤5 lines) + send/stop morph; staged text only in P1
  (attachments H2 in P3); optimistic user bubble; Enter-to-send per setting; haptic on send/error.
- Permission/question cards: NOT P1 (P2) — but thread must render `tool` parts in `awaiting` state
  as "waiting for approval (P2)" placeholder so P1 never misleads.
- Insets: composer `imePadding()` + animated IME (doc 08 §4); list behind nav bar.

## 4. Acceptance

1. Sessions list shows live server sessions incl. PC-created; search filters; status dots update via SSE.
2. New session (normal + temp w/ badge + default-temp setting honored); rename; delete (confirm per setting).
3. Chat: send → optimistic bubble → streaming agent text appends → completes with cost footer.
4. Abort mid-turn stops rendering + status returns idle. Kill-and-reopen app: thread reloads from server.
5. Airplane-mode: cached thread renders read-only + banner; send disabled with reason (X3 skeleton).
6. Tests: VM tests (send/reconcile/error with Turbine), SSE parse tests (heartbeat/delta/unknown-skip),
   MockWebServer (sessions list, prompt_async, abort). Screenshots: list, thread mid-stream, composer, temp badge.

## 5. Non-goals (P2+)

Markdown lib, permission/question cards, model/agent pickers (send uses defaults), fork/revert/share UI,
voice, attachments, widget, FGS. Optimistic send rollback only for transport errors (model errors render inline).

## 6. Review gate

Tests green · 2-emulator screenshots (incl. mid-stream) · live-serve chat round-trip from emulator
(send "ping" → agent reply renders) · grand-plan cross-check (C1–C3-subset, H1, S3) · user review.

package dev.opencode.remote.domain

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow

/** Outgoing message part (H1; file parts H2/P3 reuse File with data: URLs — doc 07 gap #1 resolved). */
data class OutPart(
    val type: String = "text",
    val text: String? = null,
    val mime: String? = null,
    val filename: String? = null,
    val url: String? = null,
)

/** Sessions + thread (C1–C3 subset, H1). Implemented in :data, consumed by :feature-chat. */
interface ChatRepository {
    val sessions: Flow<List<ChatSession>>
    val statusMap: Flow<Map<String, SessionStatus>>
    val tempSessionIds: Flow<Set<String>>
    val showTemp: Flow<Boolean>
    suspend fun refreshSessions(): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun createSession(title: String?, temp: Boolean): Result<ChatSession>
    suspend fun renameSession(id: String, title: String): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun deleteSession(id: String): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun abortSession(id: String): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun purgeTempSessions(): Result<Int>
    suspend fun setShowTemp(show: Boolean)
    suspend fun messages(sessionId: String, limit: Int = 50): Result<List<ChatMessage>>
    suspend fun send(
        sessionId: String,
        parts: List<OutPart>,
        agent: String,
        noReply: Boolean = false,
    ): Result<Unit>

    /** Live SSE event flow for the active profile (shared, reference-counted in :data). */
    val events: Flow<SseEvent>
}

/** Minimal SSE event envelope (doc 14 SSE recipe). */
data class SseEvent(
    val type: String,
    val sessionID: String? = null,
    val messageID: String? = null,
    val partID: String? = null,
    val delta: String? = null,
    val raw: String = "",
)

    fun event(type: String?, data: String): SseEvent? {
        if (type == "open") return null
        val o = runCatching { json.parseToJsonElement(data).jsonObject }.getOrNull() ?: return null
        val t = o.getStringOrNull("type") ?: type ?: return null
        if (t == "server.heartbeat" || t == "server.connected") return null
        val payload = o.getObjectOrNull("payload") ?: o.getObjectOrNull("properties") ?: o
        return SseEvent(
            type = t,
            sessionID = payload.getStringOrNull("sessionID") ?: payload.getStringOrNull("sessionId"),
            messageID = payload.getStringOrNull("messageID") ?: payload.getStringOrNull("messageId"),

# SPEC — P2 permissions / models / agents / commands / stats

Source of truth: `docs/grand-plan.md` §7. Implements: H6 (connectors view), H7 (permission cards +
allowlist doc 15 APPROVED), H8 (agent switch), H9 (model+effort picker), H10 (stats per-session;
weekly deferred — see §5), H12 (slash commands), questions (AskUserQuestion cards), markdown renderer.

## 1. Data (`:data` + `:domain`)

- `PermissionRepository` (+ domain interface): `pending: Flow<List<PermissionItem>>`,
  `refresh()` (GET /permission), `reply(id, once|always|reject)` (POST /permission/{id}/reply {reply}).
  SSE `permission.asked` → refresh; `permission.replied` → drop by requestID + refresh
  (grinev rules: failed reply stays answerable; vanished = answered elsewhere).
  `PermissionItem{id, sessionID, permission, patterns[], metadata{}, always[], tool{messageID,callID}}`
  (spec schema PermissionRequest verbatim).
- `QuestionRepository`: `pending: Flow<List<QuestionItem>>`, `refresh()` (GET /question),
  `reply(id, answers: List<List<String>>)` (labels in question order),
  `reject(id)`. SSE `question.asked/replied/rejected` same pattern.
  `QuestionItem{id, sessionID, questions[{header, question, options[{label,description}], multiple, custom}], tool?}`
  (QuestionInfo verbatim; V2 shapes parsed leniently into the same model).
- `CatalogRepository`: `providers()` (GET /provider → all[].{id,name,models{id,name,limits,modalities,cost}};
  fallback GET /config/providers), `agents()` (GET /agent, filter hidden, primary/all modes),
  `commands()` (GET /command), `mcpStatus()` (GET /mcp), `toolIds()` (GET /experimental/tool/ids, for H3 gating).
  Cache per profile in memory; refresh on profile switch + manual.
- Prompt additions: `PromptRequest` gains `model: ModelInput?`, `variant: String?`, `tools: Map<String,Boolean>?`
  (D3: H3 websearch toggle = `tools["webfetch"]=false` when off — verify tool id against /experimental/tool/ids
  at runtime, fall back to excluding nothing + note; memory toggle H5 = system-prompt injection skip, client-side).
- Stats: extend `DtoMap.message` callers — per-session totals computed in ChatViewModel from loaded
  messages (`step-finish` tokens/cost sums) + session.cost/tokens if server provides; context % =
  last assistant tokens vs selected model limit (provider map).

## 2. Thread UI (`:feature-chat`)

- Permission cards inline at the requesting turn (position: end of list while pending, like Claude):
  title/type/pattern chips + metadata filepath + Once / Always / Reject (doc 15 defaults preselected
  note: "auto-allow list would allow this" hint when applicable). After reply: card collapses to
  "allowed once ✓ / always / rejected" terminal line (grinev rule). Cross-session: cards show for the
  session open; other sessions' pending count surfaces as a badge on the sessions list (attention ids).
- Question cards: header + question + options (single → tap answers immediately; multi → toggle + Done;
  custom → text field when allowed; Cancel → reject). FIFO: newest replaces display, others queued count.
- Model+effort: top-bar chip (current model/variant) → bottom sheet: providers → models (search) →
  effort (none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max, static list per opencode config schema) → applies to next send
  + per-session memory (grapeot pattern). Favorites + recent (grinev pattern, local).
- Agent switch: chips row above composer (plan/ask/build + custom agents from /agent, hidden filtered).
  Sends `agent` per message.
- Commands: `/` in composer → autocomplete sheet (name + description) → tap appends `name + " "` or
  executes immediately if no args needed (spec: execute via POST /session/{id}/command {command, arguments};
  result renders as assistant turn). Custom + native listed together with source tag.
- Connectors (H6): overflow menu → Connectors screen: MCP server list + status (GET /mcp), toggle = P5 scope
  (view-only in P2 + note). Websearch/memory toggles as above-composer status row chips (doc 08 §7).
- Stats (H10 P2): chat header tap → sheet: session totals (in/out/reasoning, cache r/w, cost, context % bar),
  per-turn footers already present. Weekly → DEFERRED (§5).

## 3. Markdown renderer

- mikepenz `multiplatform-markdown-renderer` (`-m3` + `-code` modules): replaces MonoText; streaming via
  `rememberStreamingMarkdownState` + append (doc 08). Code blocks: language header + copy button.
  Tables, lists, links as tappable spans. Version pinned in catalog after resolve check.

## 4. Acceptance

1. Permission asked (live or simulated via unit-event) → card renders → Once/Always/Reject → terminal line;
   `permission.replied` from elsewhere removes the card.
2. Question asked → single-tap answers; multi-select + Done; custom text; cancel rejects.
3. Model sheet lists live server providers/models; pick + effort applies to next send (verify via OkHttp body).
4. Agent chips switch `agent` per send. `/` sheet lists commands; execute runs a turn.
5. Stats sheet shows session totals + context %; numbers match server cost/tokens.
6. Markdown: code fence → highlighted block + copy; table renders; links tappable.
7. Tests: DtoMap (permission/question parse), VM tests (reply/remove, model apply), MockWebServer
   (permission/question/command/provider paths + bodies). Screenshots: cards, sheets, markdown, stats.

## 5. Explicit non-goals / deferrals

- Weekly stats (H10-weekly): needs local persistence (Room) → P4 with push bridge store. DECISION recorded.
- MCP toggles, browser backend switch (P5). Voice (P3). Vim (H13 workstream). Widget (P4).
- `tools` gating exact webfetch id: runtime-resolved; if absent, H3 toggle injects "answer from chat only"
  system hint instead (fallback documented in code).

## 6. Review gate

Tests green · emulator screenshots (cards + sheets + markdown + stats) · live permission/question round-trip
if reproducible (else event-replay test) · grand-plan cross-check (H6–H10, H12, questions) · user review.

package dev.opencode.remote.domain

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow

/** A pending permission request (spec PermissionRequest verbatim, lenient). */
data class PermissionItem(
    val id: String,
    val sessionID: String,
    val permission: String,
    val patterns: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val metadata: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    val always: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val messageID: String? = null,
    val callID: String? = null,
    /** Terminal state after reply (grinev rule): null = awaiting. */
    val replied: String? = null,
)

enum class PermissionReplyKind(val wire: String) { ONCE("once"), ALWAYS("always"), REJECT("reject") }

interface PermissionRepository {
    val pending: Flow<List<PermissionItem>>
    suspend fun refresh(): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun reply(id: String, kind: PermissionReplyKind): Result<Unit>
    fun markRepliedExternally(requestID: String)
}

/** A pending AskUserQuestion request (QuestionInfo verbatim, lenient; V2 folded in). */
data class QuestionOption(val label: String, val description: String = "")

data class QuestionItem(
    val id: String,
    val sessionID: String,
    val header: String,
    val question: String,
    val options: List<QuestionOption>,
    val multiple: Boolean = false,
    val customAllowed: Boolean = false,
)

interface QuestionRepository {
    val pending: Flow<List<QuestionItem>>
    suspend fun refresh(): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun reply(id: String, answers: List<List<String>>): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun reject(id: String): Result<Unit>
    fun markSettledExternally(requestID: String)
}

/** Provider/model/agent/command catalogs (server-driven pickers). */
data class ModelInfo(
    val id: String,
    val name: String,
    val contextLimit: Long = 0,
)

data class ProviderInfo(
    val id: String,
    val name: String,
    val models: List<ModelInfo>,
)

data class AgentInfo(
    val name: String,
    val description: String = "",
    val mode: String = "all",
)

data class CommandInfo(
    val name: String,
    val description: String = "",
    val source: String = "",
)

data class McpServerInfo(
    val name: String,
    val status: String,
)

interface CatalogRepository {
    val providers: Flow<List<ProviderInfo>>
    val agents: Flow<List<AgentInfo>>
    val commands: Flow<List<CommandInfo>>
    val mcpServers: Flow<List<McpServerInfo>>
    val toolIds: Flow<List<String>>
    suspend fun refresh(): Result<Unit>
}

/** Per-session model/agent/effort memory (grapeot pattern). */
data class SessionPrefs(
    val modelID: String? = null,
    val providerID: String? = null,
    val variant: String? = null,
    val agent: String? = null,
)

# multiplatform-markdown-renderer

[](#multiplatform-markdown-renderer)

Render Markdown as native Compose UI — one API, every platform.

[![CI status](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/actions) [![Maven Central version](https://camo.githubusercontent.)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/com.mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://camo.githubusercontent.)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer) [![Apache 2.0 license](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/f33da71a29405001aa02da9ecc600166564fbf91b075090f06daf1a0012969a3/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f6c6963656e73652d417061636865253230322e302d626c75653f7374796c653d666c61742d737175617265)](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/blob/develop/LICENSE)

 ![A markdown String is parsed by JetBrains Markdown into an AST, mapped through overridable MarkdownComponents, and rendered as Compose Multiplatform UI on Android, iOS, Desktop, Web and macOS.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/develop/art/hero-light.svg)

[Quickstart](#quickstart) • [Showcase](#showcase) • [Reference](#reference) • [Migration](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/blob/develop/MIGRATION.md) • [Changelog](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/blob/develop/CHANGELOG.md)

🧩 **Every platform**

Android, iOS, Desktop (JVM), Web (Wasm / JS) and macOS from one `commonMain` call.

⚡ **Async by default**

`rememberMarkdownState` parses off the composition; `retainState = true` keeps content visible while re-parsing.

🎨 **Material 2 and 3**

Themed defaults from `-m2` / `-m3`; override with `markdownColor()` and `markdownTypography()`.

🧱 **Every element overridable**

`MarkdownComponents` maps each AST node to a `@Composable` you control.

📊 **Full GFM**

Tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and GitHub alerts, out of the box.

📡 **Built for streaming**

`rememberStreamingMarkdownState()` appends chunks and re-parses only the unstable tail.

## Quickstart

[](#quickstart)

**1 — Add the dependency.** Pick the module matching your Material theme:

dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer:0.43.0")
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m3:0.43.0") // or -m2
}

**2 — Render.** Import `Markdown` from `com.mikepenz.markdown.m3` (or `.m2`):

import com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.Markdown

Markdown(
    """
    # Hello Markdown
    - Bullet points
    - \*\*Bold\*\* and \*italic\* text
    \[Check out this link\](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer)
    """.trimIndent()
)

**3 — Hoist the parse for anything non-trivial.** `rememberMarkdownState` parses asynchronously and survives recomposition:

val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown)
Markdown(markdownState)

Full configuration — custom components, image loading, syntax highlighting, extended spans — is in the [Reference](#reference) below.

### What's included 🚀

[](#whats-included-)

-   **Cross-platform Markdown Rendering** - Works on Android, iOS, Desktop, and Web
-   **Material Design Integration** - Seamless integration with Material 2 and Material 3 themes
-   **Rich Markdown Support** - Renders headings, lists, code blocks, tables, images, and more
-   **Syntax Highlighting** - Optional code syntax highlighting for various programming languages
-   **Image Loading** - Flexible image loading with Coil2 and Coil3 integration
-   **Customization Options** - Extensive customization for colors, typography, components, and more

-   **Extended Text Spans** - Support for advanced text styling with extended spans
-   **Lightweight** - Minimal dependencies and optimized for performance

## Setup

[](#setup)

### Using Gradle

[](#using-gradle)

Choose the appropriate configuration based on your project type:

**Multiplatform**

For multiplatform projects, add these dependencies to your `build.gradle.kts`:

dependencies {
    // Core library
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer:${version}")

    // Choose ONE of the following based on your Material theme:

    // For Material 2 themed apps
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m2:${version}")

    // OR for Material 3 themed apps
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m3:${version}")
}

**JVM (Desktop)**

For JVM-only projects, add this dependency:

dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-jvm:${version}")
}

**Android**

For Android-only projects, add this dependency:

dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-android:${version}")
}

Important

Since version 0.13.0, the core library does not depend on a Material theme. You must include either the `-m2` or `-m3` module to get access to the default styling.

## Usage

[](#usage)

### Basic Usage

[](#basic-usage)

The most basic usage is to simply pass your markdown string to the `Markdown` composable:

// In your composable (use the appropriate Markdown implementation for your theme)
Markdown(
    """
    # Hello Markdown
    This is a simple markdown example with:
    - Bullet points
    - \*\*Bold text\*\*
    - \*Italic text\*
    \[Check out this link\](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer)
    """.trimIndent()
)

Note

Import either `com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.Markdown` for Material 3 or `com.mikepenz.markdown.m2.Markdown` for Material 2 themed applications.

Note

By default, when the markdown `content` changes, the component will display a loading state while parsing the new content. To keep the previous content visible during updates and avoid showing the loading state, set `retainState` to `true`.

**Advanced Usage**

### `rememberMarkdownState`

[](#remembermarkdownstate)

For better performance, especially with larger markdown content, use `rememberMarkdownState` or move the parsing of the markdown into your viewmodel:

val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown)
Markdown(markdownState)

> \[!NOTE\]  
> Since version 0.33.0, markdown content is parsed asynchronously by default, resulting in a loading state being displayed prior to the parsing result. The `rememberMarkdownState` function offers the ability to require immediate parsing with the `immediate` parameter, but this is not advised as it might block the composition of the UI.

// Default asynchronous parsing (recommended)
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown)

// Force immediate parsing (not recommended)
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown, immediate \= true)

#### Retaining State During Updates

[](#retaining-state-during-updates)

By default, when the markdown content changes, the component shows a loading state while parsing the new content. You can use the `retainState` parameter to keep the previous rendered content visible while the new content is being parsed:

// Retain previous content during updates (avoids showing loading state)
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(
    markdown,
    retainState \= true
)
Markdown(markdownState)

// With dynamic content loading
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(
    key, // key that triggers re-parsing
    retainState \= true
) {
    "\# Dynamic content $counter"
}
Markdown(markdownState)

This is particularly useful when content updates frequently or when you want to avoid flickering between the old content and the loading state.

### Lazy Loading for Large Documents

[](#lazy-loading-for-large-documents)

Since version 0.33.0, the library supports rendering large markdown documents efficiently using `LazyColumn` instead of `Column`. This is particularly useful for very long markdown content.

Markdown(
    markdownState \= markdownState,
    success \= { state, components, modifier \->
        LazyMarkdownSuccess(state, components, modifier, contentPadding \= PaddingValues(16.dp))
    },
    modifier \= Modifier.fillMaxSize()
)

### Parse Markdown in VM

[](#parse-markdown-in-vm)

> \[!NOTE\]  
> This approach is also advised if you want to retain scroll position even when navigating away See: [#374](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/issues/374) Retaining state in the VM ensures parsing will not have to be done again, and the component can be immediately filled.

// In the VM setup the flow to parse the markdown
val markdownFlow \= parseMarkdownFlow("\# Markdown")
    .stateIn(lifecycleScope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, State.Loading())

// In the Composable use the flow
val state by markdownFlow.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
Markdown(state)

### Parse Markdown synchronously

[](#parse-markdown-synchronously)

If you want to pre-parse content before showing the UI and hand the result to `Markdown` without any Flow/StateFlow machinery, use `parseMarkdown`. It parses on the calling thread and returns the final, immutable `State` directly (`State.Success` on success, or `State.Error` on failure).

// Parse ahead of time and pass the already-parsed state to the Composable
val state \= parseMarkdown("\# Markdown")
Markdown(state)

> \[!NOTE\]  
> Parsing happens on the calling thread. For large documents consider invoking this off the main thread.

The library offers the ability to modify different behaviour when rendering the markdown.

### Provided custom style

[](#provided-custom-style)

Markdown(
    content,
    colors \= markdownColor(text \= Color.Red),
    typography \= markdownTypography(h1 \= MaterialTheme.typography.body1)
)

### Disable Animation

[](#disable-animation)

By default, the `MarkdownText` animates size changes (if images are loaded).

Markdown(
    content,
    animations \= markdownAnimations(
        animateTextSize \= {
            this
            /\*\* No animation \*/
        }
    ),
)

### Extended spans

[](#extended-spans)

Starting with 0.16.0 the library includes support for [extended-spans](https://github.com/saket/extended-spans).

> The library was integrated to make it multiplatform-compatible. All credits for its functionality go to [Saket Narayan](https://github.com/saket).

It is not enabled by default, however you can enable it quickly by configuring the `extendedSpans` for your `Markdown` composeable. Define the `ExtendedSpans` you want to apply (including optionally your own custom ones) and return it.

Markdown(
    content,
    extendedSpans \= markdownExtendedSpans {
        val animator \= rememberSquigglyUnderlineAnimator()
        remember {
            ExtendedSpans(
                RoundedCornerSpanPainter(),
                SquigglyUnderlineSpanPainter(animator \= animator)
            )
        }
    }
)

### Extend Annotated string handling

[](#extend-annotated-string-handling)

The library already handles a significant amount of different tokens, however not all. To allow special integrations expand this, you can pass in a custom `annotator` to the `Markdown` composeable. This `annotator` allows you to customize existing handled tokens, but also add new ones.

Markdown(
    content,
    annotator \= markdownAnnotator { content, child \->
        if (child.type \== GFMElementTypes.STRIKETHROUGH) {
            append("Replaced you :)")
            true // return true to consume this ASTNode child
        } else false
    }
)

### Adjust List Ordering

[](#adjust-list-ordering)

// Use the bullet list symbol from the original markdown
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalBulletListHandler provides { type, bullet, index, listNumber, depth \-> "$bullet " }) {
    Markdown(content)
}

// Replace the ordered list symbol with \`A.)\` instead.
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalOrderedListHandler provides { type, bullet, index, listNumber, depth \-> "A.) " }) {
    Markdown(content, Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp).verticalScroll(scrollState))
}

### Custom Components

[](#custom-components)

Since v0.9.0 it is possible to provide custom components, instead of the default ones. This can be done by providing the components `MarkdownComponents` to the `Markdown` composable.

Use the `markdownComponents()` to keep defaults for non overwritten components.

The `MarkdownComponent` will expose access to the `content: String`, `node: ASTNode`, `typography: MarkdownTypography`, offering full flexibility.

// Simple adjusted paragraph with different Modifier.
val customParagraphComponent: MarkdownComponent \= {
    Box(modifier \= Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
        MarkdownParagraph(it.content, it.node, Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterEnd))
    }
}

// Full custom paragraph example 
val customParagraphComponentComplex: MarkdownComponent \= {
    // build a styled paragraph. (util function provided by the library)
    val styledText \= buildAnnotatedString {
        pushStyle(LocalMarkdownTypography.current.paragraph.toSpanStyle())
        buildMarkdownAnnotatedString(it.content, it.node, annotatorSettings())
        pop()
    }

    // define the \`Text\` composable
    Text(
        styledText,
        textAlign \= TextAlign.End
    )
}

// Define the \`Markdown\` composable and pass in the custom paragraph component
Markdown(
    content,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        paragraph \= customParagraphComponent // customParagraphComponentComplex
    )
)

Another example to of a custom component is changing the rendering of an unordered list.

// Define a custom component for rendering unordered list items in Markdown
val customUnorderedListComponent: MarkdownComponent \= {
    // Use the MarkdownListItems composable to render the list items
    MarkdownListItems(it.content, it.node, depth \= 0) { startNumber, index, child \->
        // Render an icon for the bullet point with a green tint
        Icon(
            imageVector \= icon,
            tint \= Color.Green,
            contentDescription \= null,
            modifier \= Modifier.size(20.dp),
        )
    }
}

// Define the \`Markdown\` composable and pass in the custom unorderedList component
Markdown(
    content,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        unorderedList \= customUnorderedListComponent
    )
)

### Table Support

[](#table-support)

Starting with 0.30.0, the library includes support for rendering tables in markdown. The `Markdown` composable will automatically handle table elements in your markdown content.

val markdown \= """
| Header 1 | Header 2 |
|----------|----------|
| Cell 1   | Cell 2   |
| Cell 3   | Cell 4   |
""".trimIndent()

Markdown(markdown)

### Alert Support

[](#alert-support)

The library renders [GitHub alerts](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/16925) — `NOTE`, `TIP`, `IMPORTANT`, `WARNING` and `CAUTION` — as an accent bar with an icon and a title.

val markdown \= """
\> \[!NOTE\]
\> Useful information that users should know, even when skimming content.
""".trimIndent()

Markdown(markdown)

The accent colors, dimensions and paddings are grouped into dedicated models, the title style is exposed via `markdownTypography(alertTitle = ...)`:

Markdown(
    markdown,
    colors \= markdownColor(alert \= markdownAlertColors(note \= Color.Blue)),
    dimens \= markdownDimens(alert \= markdownAlertDimens(barThickness \= 2.dp)),
    padding \= markdownPadding(alert \= markdownAlertPadding(iconSpacing \= 12.dp)),
)

The icons are swappable via `LocalMarkdownAlertIcons`:

CompositionLocalProvider(
    LocalMarkdownAlertIcons provides markdownAlertIcons(note \= Icons.Outlined.Info)
) {
    Markdown(markdown)
}

To fully replace the rendering, override the `alert` component through `markdownComponents()`.

## Streaming

[](#streaming)

For content that arrives in chunks — an LLM response, a network stream — use `rememberStreamingMarkdownState()`. It is append-only: each `append` re-parses only the unstable tail of the document rather than the whole string.

val streamingMarkdownState \= rememberStreamingMarkdownState()

LaunchedEffect(chunkFlow) {
    chunkFlow.collect { chunk \-> streamingMarkdownState.append(chunk) }
}

Markdown(streamingMarkdownState \= streamingMarkdownState)

If the chunks already arrive as a `Flow<String>`, `collectAsStreamingMarkdownState()` does the collecting for you:

val streamingMarkdownState \= chunkFlow.collectAsStreamingMarkdownState()
Markdown(streamingMarkdownState \= streamingMarkdownState)

`StreamingMarkdownState.snapshot` exposes the split as a `StateFlow<Snapshot>` with `stableAst` and `unstableAstTail`, if you need to observe it. See `StreamingMarkDownPage` in the sample for a working example including render statistics.

### Image Loading

[](#image-loading)

To configure image loading, the library offers different implementations, to offer great flexibility for the respective integration. After adding the dependency, the chosen image transformer implementation has to be passed to the `Markdown` API.

Note

Please refer to the official documentation for the specific image loading integration you are using (e.g., coil3) on how to adjust its behavior.

#### coil3

[](#coil3)

// Offers coil3 (Coil3ImageTransformerImpl)
implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-coil3:${version}")

Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    imageTransformer \= Coil3ImageTransformerImpl,
)

#### coil2

[](#coil2)

// Offers coil2 (Coil2ImageTransformerImpl)
implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-coil2:${version}")

Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    imageTransformer \= Coil2ImageTransformerImpl,
)

### Syntax Highlighting

[](#syntax-highlighting)

The library (introduced with 0.27.0) offers optional support for syntax highlighting via the [Highlights](https://github.com/SnipMeDev/Highlights) project. This support is not included in the core, and can be enabled by adding the `multiplatform-markdown-renderer-code` dependency.

implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-code:${version}")

Once added, the `Markdown` has to be configured to use the alternative code highlighter.

// Use default color scheme
Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        codeBlock \= highlightedCodeBlock,
        codeFence \= highlightedCodeFence,
    )
)

// ADVANCED: Customize Highlights library by defining different theme
val isDarkTheme \= isSystemInDarkTheme()
val highlightsBuilder \= remember(isDarkTheme) {
    Highlights.Builder().theme(SyntaxThemes.atom(darkMode \= isDarkTheme))
}
Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        codeBlock \= {
            MarkdownHighlightedCodeBlock(
                content \= it.content,
                node \= it.node,
                highlightsBuilder \= highlightsBuilder,
                showHeader \= true, // optional enable header with code language + copy button
            )
        },
        codeFence \= {
            MarkdownHighlightedCodeFence(
                content \= it.content,
                node \= it.node,
                highlightsBuilder \= highlightsBuilder,
                showHeader \= true, // optional enable header with code language + copy button
            )
        },
    )
)

    content: String,
    colors: MarkdownColors,
    typography: MarkdownTypography,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(),
    padding: MarkdownPadding = markdownPadding(),
    dimens: MarkdownDimens = markdownDimens(),

package dev.opencode.remote.chat

import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.mikepenz.markdown.compose.Markdown
import com.mikepenz.markdown.compose.components.markdownComponents
import com.mikepenz.markdown.compose.elements.highlightedCodeFence
import com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.markdownColor
import com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.markdownTypography

/**
 * Agent text renderer (P2): full markdown (tables, lists, links, GFM alerts) +
 * highlighted code fences with language header + copy button (spec §3).
 * 0.41.0 pinned: last line readable by Kotlin 2.2 (stdlib 2.3.21); no streaming
 * state API in this line, so updates re-parse with retained state (no flicker).
 */
@Composable
fun MarkdownText(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val components = remember {
        markdownComponents(codeFence = highlightedCodeFence)
    }
    Markdown(
        content = text,
        colors = markdownColor(),
        typography = markdownTypography(),
        components = components,
        retainState = true,
        modifier = modifier,
    )
}

# SPEC — P3 attachments / voice / projects / vim

Source of truth: `docs/grand-plan.md` §7. Implements: H2 (attachments), H4-dictation (voice mode deferred —
see §5), H5 (memory toggle wiring), H11 (projects per D1), H13 kickoff (vim scope + spike, non-blocking).

## 1. Attachments (H2)

- Composer `+` button → sheet: Take photo (CameraX or `TakePicture` contract) / Choose image (Photo Picker,
  no storage perm) / Choose file (SAF `OpenDocument`, any mime).
- Staging: chips above composer with thumb/name/size + × remove. Images downscaled + JPEG-compressed
  client-side per settings (max dimension, quality) BEFORE base64; files ≤ setting cap (default 10MB,
  refuse larger with reason). HEIC/PNG → JPEG convert for photos.
- Send: `FilePartInput{type:"file", mime, filename, url:"data:<mime>;base64,..."}` appended after the
  text part (doc 07 probe: verified round-trip). Mixed text+files in one `prompt_async`.
- Thread render: image parts → Coil thumbnail, tap → zoom/pan viewer (P3 basic viewer: full-screen
  pan/zoom, share via system sheet). Non-image files → file card (name/mime).
- Settings honored: image compression (off/light/medium), max dimension, camera resolution.

## 2. Voice dictation (H4-dictation)

- Composer mic button → platform `SpeechRecognizer` (on-device if available) with partial results
  streamed into the composer text; error states (no speech, no permission) inline.
  Runtime `RECORD_AUDIO` request with rationale (X5 aggressive list covers it).
- Full-duplex voice MODE (conversation) → DEFERRED (§5): needs TTS + turn-taking + audio session
  management; own workstream after P4.

## 3. Projects (H11, D1)

- Client-side `Project` entity: `{id, name, directories[], instructions, memoryNote}` stored in
  DataStore (Room deferred to P4; DataStore JSON list suffices for P3 scale).
- Sessions screen: project filter chips (All + projects); new-session sheet offers project attach
  (sets default directory + injects instructions/memory as `system` prompt on first send of session).
- Projects manager screen (from Sessions overflow): CRUD + directory multi-add (via server `/project`
  worktree picker) + instructions/memory editors.
- H5 memory toggle: per-message effect = include/exclude the project's memoryNote (+ global simple-memory
  note TBD) from the `system` injection. Composer status row shows memory chip state (chip UI in P3,
  injection log line in debug).

## 4. Vim workstream kickoff (H13, non-blocking)

- Spike: survey Compose vim options (no known mature lib — expect custom `InputConnection` wrapper
  around the composer `TextFieldValue` + mode state machine). Deliverable: `docs/vim-spike.md` with
  approach + effort estimate + maximal-scope breakdown (normal/insert/visual, motions+text objects,
  registers, macros, marks/jumps, `:s`, counts). NO composer changes in P3 (parallel track).

## 5. Explicit non-goals / deferrals

- Voice MODE (full duplex), audio messages (record/play) → post-P4 workstream.
- Room (weekly stats store, message cache) → P4 with push bridge.
- Vim implementation → own workstream after spike approval.
- Image zoom viewer: basic pan/zoom + share in P3; annotate/crop later.

## 6. Acceptance

1. Photo → staged chip → send → server thread shows file part (verify via GET message mime/filename).
2. Gallery image + SAF file stage/send the same way; oversize file refused with reason.
3. Compression settings change resulting upload bytes (spot-check sizes).
4. Mic → dictated text appears in composer; denied perm → rationale + settings deep-link.
5. Project CRUD; session attached to project sends with `system` injection (verify via OkHttp body log).
6. Memory toggle flips injection on/off.
7. Vim spike doc written with estimate; no composer regression (existing tests green).
8. Tests: compression/staging VM tests, project repo tests, MockWebServer (file part body shape).
   Screenshots: attach sheet, staged chips, viewer, dictation, projects screens.

## 7. Review gate

Tests green · emulator screenshots · live file-part round-trip vs server · grand-plan cross-check
(H2, H4-dictation, H5, H11, H13-spike) · user review.
